label: Blues---Boogie Woogie
description: Piano-driven blues with rolling left-hand patterns, upbeat rhythm, and strong dance energy.
classificationHint: Use this when the piano rhythm is fast, repetitive, and boogie-based.

label: Blues---Chicago Blues
description: Urban electric blues associated with amplified guitar, harmonica, full band arrangements, and a strong city blues feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has electric blues band sound rather than rural acoustic blues.

label: Blues---Country Blues
description: Rural acoustic blues style with guitar-led accompaniment, direct vocals, and folk-like looseness.
classificationHint: Use this when the recording feels acoustic, rural, and solo or small-ensemble blues.

label: Blues---Delta Blues
description: Early Mississippi Delta blues style with raw vocals, slide guitar, and sparse acoustic performance.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has stark acoustic blues character and Delta-style phrasing.

label: Blues---East Coast Blues
description: An East Coast and southeastern acoustic blues tradition closely associated with Piedmont fingerpicking, using alternating-thumb bass beneath syncopated, ragtime-like treble figures.
classificationHint: Use this regional umbrella when agile acoustic fingerstyle and ragtime-derived syncopation point to the eastern Piedmont tradition but a narrower local label is not justified.

label: Blues---Electric Blues
description: Blues performed with amplified instruments, especially electric guitar, bass, drums, and harmonica.
classificationHint: Use this when electric instrumentation defines the blues sound but no regional electric style is clearer.

label: Blues---Harmonica Blues
description: Blues where harmonica is a central lead or response instrument.
classificationHint: Use this when blues harp lines are one of the main identifying elements.

label: Blues---Jump Blues
description: Up-tempo blues with swing rhythm, horn sections, and strong dance-band energy.
classificationHint: Use this when the track sits between blues, swing, and early rhythm and blues.

label: Blues---Louisiana Blues
description: A Louisiana regional blues umbrella shaped by New Orleans rhythm and blues, Gulf Coast piano and horn traditions, and the relaxed guitar-led swamp-blues sound of southern Louisiana.
classificationHint: Use this when Louisiana rhythmic, vocal, or ensemble character is identifiable but the recording is not better classified as a specific New Orleans R&B or swamp style.

label: Blues---Memphis Blues
description: Blues from the Memphis and Beale Street tradition, spanning jug-band and vaudeville roots through electric guitar, piano, horns, and a strong bridge toward soul and rhythm and blues.
classificationHint: Use this when Memphis regional character is evident in a compact, rhythmically lively blues arrangement with jug-band, piano, horn, or electric Beale Street lineage.

label: Blues---Modern Electric Blues
description: Contemporary amplified blues using modern electric-guitar tone, full rhythm-section production, and often stronger rock influence while retaining blues form, phrasing, and improvisation.
classificationHint: Use this when polished modern amplification and guitar-led production distinguish the track from older regional electric blues, but it remains fundamentally blues rather than blues rock.

label: Blues---Piano Blues
description: Blues centered on piano accompaniment, riffs, and vocal-piano interaction.
classificationHint: Use this when piano is the main blues instrument rather than guitar or harmonica.

label: Blues---Piedmont Blues
description: A southeastern acoustic guitar style where a steady alternating-thumb bass supports syncopated treble melody, creating a flowing fingerpicked texture influenced by ragtime.
classificationHint: Use this when alternating-thumb fingerpicking and independent syncopated treble lines are the defining feature, rather than Delta-style slide guitar or a strummed country-blues approach.

label: Blues---Rhythm & Blues
description: Blues-related style with stronger groove, backbeat, and early R&B song structure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track bridges blues and rhythm-and-blues rather than sounding like pure blues.

label: Blues---Texas Blues
description: A Texas guitar-blues lineage ranging from swinging, jazz-informed electric phrasing to later high-powered blues-rock, typically centered on expressive lead guitar and a firm danceable groove.
classificationHint: Use this when guitar tone and phrasing carry a recognizable Texas blend of blues, swing, and rock energy rather than Chicago-style harmonica-and-band emphasis.

label: Brass & Military---Brass Band
description: Music performed by an ensemble dominated by brass instruments with percussion, including British-style contest bands, New Orleans brass bands, Balkan brass ensembles, civic bands, and other regionally distinct traditions.
classificationHint: Use when brass-band ensemble identity is central; Marches describe a musical form or function, Military requires military context, and Pipe & Drum uses bagpipes with drums rather than a brass core.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Marches
distinguishFrom.difference: Brass Band identifies the ensemble; Marches identify music structured for marching and can be played by many ensembles.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Military
distinguishFrom.difference: Brass Band identifies instrumentation; Military identifies institutional or ceremonial military context.

label: Brass & Military---Marches
description: Music composed or adapted for coordinated walking or procession, usually in a regular duple meter with clear repeated strains and emphatic cadence, performed by military, civic, brass, wind, pipe, or orchestral ensembles.
classificationHint: Use when march form and locomotor function are audible or documented; a brass-band recording is not automatically a march, and Military requires institutional context.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Brass Band
distinguishFrom.difference: Marches identify form and function; Brass Band identifies the performing ensemble.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Military
distinguishFrom.difference: Marches may be civic, ceremonial, theatrical, or military; Military specifically identifies armed-forces context.

label: Brass & Military---Military
description: A functional umbrella for music of armed-forces bands, ceremonial units, buglers, field musicians, and military institutions, including signals, honors, marches, parade music, and commemorative repertory.
classificationHint: Use when military provenance or ceremonial function is explicit; instrumentation or march rhythm alone is insufficient because civic brass and pipe bands perform similar repertory.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Marches
distinguishFrom.difference: Military identifies institutional context; Marches identify a musical form that also exists outside the military.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Brass Band
distinguishFrom.difference: Military identifies function and affiliation; Brass Band identifies instrumentation and ensemble type.

label: Brass & Military---Pipe & Drum
description: Ensemble music centered on bagpipes and drums, commonly snare, tenor, and bass drums, for parade, ceremonial, competition, regimental, or community performance in Scottish and related pipe-band traditions.
classificationHint: Use when coordinated bagpipe-and-drum ensemble sound defines the recording; solo piping, brass marching bands, and generic Military music need their own labels.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Brass Band
distinguishFrom.difference: Pipe & Drum is centered on bagpipes and percussion; Brass Band is centered on brass instruments.

distinguishFrom.label: Brass & Military---Military
distinguishFrom.difference: Pipe & Drum identifies an ensemble type that may be military or civilian; Military requires institutional context.

label: Children's---Educational
description: Music, songs, stories, exercises, or spoken instruction created specifically to teach children concepts, language, numbers, social skills, movement, or other age-appropriate knowledge.
classificationHint: Use when young learners and an explicit teaching goal are central; Non-Music Education targets general audiences, while Nursery Rhymes may entertain or support memory without a structured lesson.

distinguishFrom.label: Non-Music---Education
distinguishFrom.difference: Children’s Educational is explicitly designed for young learners; Non-Music Education is the general instructional category.

distinguishFrom.label: Children's---Nursery Rhymes
distinguishFrom.difference: Children’s Educational has a defined teaching objective; Nursery Rhymes are traditional or tradition-like short children’s verses and songs.

label: Children's---Nursery Rhymes
description: Short traditional or tradition-like verses and songs for young children, characterized by memorable rhyme, repetition, simple melody, wordplay, actions, counting, or game function.
classificationHint: Use for recognizable nursery-rhyme form or repertory; not every children’s song is a Nursery Rhyme, and Educational requires an explicit teaching purpose.

distinguishFrom.label: Children's---Educational
distinguishFrom.difference: Nursery Rhymes are a specific short verse/song tradition; Educational audio is defined by a teaching objective.

distinguishFrom.label: Children's---Story
distinguishFrom.difference: Nursery Rhymes are brief repetitive verses or songs; Story uses extended narrative with characters and events.

label: Children's---Story
description: Narrated or dramatized fiction and traditional tales made for children, using characters, events, and an age-appropriate narrative arc, with optional voices, songs, music, and sound effects.
classificationHint: Use when children’s narrative is primary; Audiobook is tied to a published or book-length work regardless of age, while Nursery Rhymes are short repetitive verse forms.

distinguishFrom.label: Non-Music---Audiobook
distinguishFrom.difference: Children’s Story is defined by audience and narrative content; Audiobook is defined by narration of a book-length written work.

distinguishFrom.label: Children's---Nursery Rhymes
distinguishFrom.difference: Story develops an extended narrative; Nursery Rhymes are brief repetitive verses or songs.

label: Classical---Baroque
description: Classical music from or imitating the Baroque era, often using counterpoint, basso continuo, and ornate melodic movement.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece has Baroque instrumentation or style, such as Bach-like counterpoint, harpsichord, or dance-suite character.

label: Classical---Choral
description: Classical music centered on choir or multiple vocal parts.
classificationHint: Use this when choral singing is the main musical body.

label: Classical---Classical
description: Music from or modeled on the Classical period, with balanced forms, clear harmony, and elegant orchestral or chamber writing.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece sounds Classical-era but not more specifically opera, choral, or other listed forms.

label: Classical---Contemporary
description: Recent or modern classical composition using current concert-music language.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece belongs to contemporary classical practice rather than pop, score, or ambient.

label: Classical---Early
description: A broad repertory category for Western art music before the Classical era, especially Medieval and Renaissance music and, in some usage, historically performed Baroque works.
classificationHint: Use this broad label when pre-Classical modes, instruments, or historically informed performance are clear but a narrower Medieval, Renaissance, or Baroque tag is uncertain.

label: Classical---Impressionist
description: Classical music with coloristic harmony, fluid rhythm, and atmospheric texture associated with Impressionism.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece emphasizes mood, color, and blurred harmony over strong classical development.

label: Classical---Medieval
description: European art and sacred music from roughly the ninth through fifteenth centuries, encompassing monophonic chant, organum, troubadour and trouvère song, ars antiqua and ars nova polyphony, and period instrumental dance repertory.
classificationHint: Use for historically grounded medieval repertory or performance practice; Early is the broader time-spanning umbrella, while Renaissance favors later imitative polyphony, fuller part writing, and different secular forms.

distinguishFrom.label: Classical---Early
distinguishFrom.difference: Medieval names a specific historical period and repertory; Early is the broader umbrella that can also include Renaissance and other pre-Baroque music.

distinguishFrom.label: Classical---Renaissance
distinguishFrom.difference: Medieval includes chant, early polyphony, and courtly song; Renaissance more often uses mature imitative polyphony and later vocal/instrumental forms.

label: Classical---Modern
description: Twentieth-century classical music with modern harmonic, rhythmic, or formal language.
classificationHint: Use this when the music is classical but not tonal/romantic in a traditional way.

label: Classical---Neo-Classical
description: A twentieth-century modernist return to Classical and Baroque ideals of clarity, balance, economy, contrapuntal texture, and established forms, often with updated harmony and rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this when modern musical language deliberately adopts older formal models and restrained, transparent writing rather than Romantic expansiveness.

label: Classical---Neo-Romantic
description: Modern or contemporary classical music that renews nineteenth-century Romantic traits such as lyrical melody, rich harmony, dramatic buildup, and direct personal expression.
classificationHint: Use this when a work written beyond the Romantic period deliberately restores tonal, emotionally expansive Romantic language within a later compositional setting.

label: Classical---Opera
description: Dramatic classical vocal music for staged narrative, usually with trained operatic voices and orchestral support.
classificationHint: Use this when operatic singing and dramatic stage form are central.

label: Classical---Operetta
description: Light opera with spoken dialogue, accessible melodies, and theatrical entertainment character.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece sounds like lighter staged classical theatre rather than full opera.

label: Classical---Oratorio
description: Large-scale sacred or dramatic classical vocal work, usually unstaged, with choir, soloists, and orchestra.
classificationHint: Use this when choral/orchestral vocal writing resembles a concert religious or dramatic work.

label: Classical---Post-Modern
description: Late-twentieth-century classical music that rejects a single modernist language through stylistic pluralism, quotation, historical reference, tonal return, collage, irony, or crossover.
classificationHint: Use this when deliberate mixing of eras, idioms, or high-and-popular culture is structurally central; do not use it merely because a contemporary work is eclectic.

label: Classical---Renaissance
description: European classical music from or imitating the Renaissance era, often with modal harmony and vocal polyphony.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece has Renaissance choral or early-instrument character.

label: Classical---Romantic
description: Classical music emphasizing emotional expression, expanded harmony, and dramatic orchestral or piano writing.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece has 19th-century romantic expression rather than classical restraint.

label: Classical---Twelve-tone
description: Modern classical music using twelve-tone or serial pitch organization.
classificationHint: Use this when the piece sounds atonal or serial and avoids normal tonal center.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Experimental
distinguishFrom.difference: Experimental emphasizes boundary-pushing method or intent; Abstract emphasizes unusual form, texture, or non-direct structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Leftfield
distinguishFrom.difference: Leftfield is unusual but can still be groove- or song-based; Abstract is more textural, fragmented, or non-functional.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient focuses on atmosphere and space; Abstract may be less immersive and more conceptually or structurally unusual.

label: Electronic---Abstract
description: Electronic music focused on unusual structure, texture, or concept rather than direct dance function.
classificationHint: Use this when the track sounds experimental, fragmented, or textural and does not fit a clear club style.

label: Electronic---Acid
description: Electronic music built around the squelchy, resonant sound associated with acid-style bass synthesis.
classificationHint: Use this when the defining feature is an acid bassline or acidic synth pattern, even if the rhythm sits in house, techno, or trance territory.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Acid House
distinguishFrom.difference: Acid House is specifically house-based; Acid can describe the acid sound across multiple electronic styles.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno may be driving and repetitive without the distinct squelchy acid bass character.

label: Electronic---Acid House
description: House music centered on squelchy acid basslines, repetitive grooves, and a raw club feel.
classificationHint: Use this for house-tempo tracks where the acid bassline is the main identity of the track.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and may not contain the characteristic acid bass sound.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Acid
distinguishFrom.difference: Acid House is more specifically tied to a house groove and tempo.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is usually harder, more linear, and less house-groove oriented.

label: Electronic---Acid Jazz
description: A groove-oriented style combining jazz, funk, soul, and electronic or club production influences.
classificationHint: Use this when jazz harmony, live-feeling grooves, and funk/soul rhythm are central, but the production has a club or electronic edge.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Future Jazz
distinguishFrom.difference: Future Jazz is usually more electronic and modern in texture; Acid Jazz often feels funkier and more band-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Jazz---Jazz-Funk
distinguishFrom.difference: Jazz-Funk is usually less tied to electronic or club production.

label: Electronic---Ambient
description: Atmospheric electronic music focused on tone, space, and mood rather than beat-driven structure.
classificationHint: Use this for slow or beatless tracks built from pads, drones, field-like textures, or immersive sound design.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drone
distinguishFrom.difference: Drone is usually more static and sustained; Ambient can have more harmonic movement and atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Age
distinguishFrom.difference: New Age is often softer, spiritual, or relaxation-oriented; Ambient can be more neutral, abstract, or experimental.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Dark Ambient emphasizes ominous, bleak, or threatening atmosphere.

label: Electronic---Baltimore Club
description: A fast, sample-heavy club style with chopped vocal hits, breakbeats, and a raw party rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this for energetic club tracks with repeated vocal chops, breakbeat pressure, and a direct dancefloor feel.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ghetto House
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghetto House is more house-based and often more minimal; Baltimore Club relies heavily on chopped breaks and vocal stabs.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Juke
distinguishFrom.difference: Juke is usually faster and more syncopated, with a stronger Chicago footwork connection.

label: Electronic---Bassline
description: UK club music centered on prominent bass hooks, garage-influenced rhythm, and energetic dancefloor bounce.
classificationHint: Use this when the bassline carries the track and the rhythm feels close to UK garage or speed garage.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speed Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: Speed Garage usually has a more obvious garage swing and organ/bass wobble; Bassline can be more direct and modern.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---UK Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: UK Garage is broader and often smoother or more vocal-led.

label: Electronic---Beatdown
description: A deep, raw, slow-burning house or techno-related style with heavy groove and understated repetition.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is electronic, groove-heavy, and stripped back, with a rough or underground feel rather than bright hooks.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep House
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep House is usually smoother and warmer; Beatdown often feels rougher and more reduced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Minimal
distinguishFrom.difference: Minimal focuses on sparse repetition; Beatdown keeps a heavier groove feel.

label: Electronic---Berlin-School
description: Sequencer-driven electronic music with long-form patterns, cosmic synth textures, and gradual development.
classificationHint: Use this for analog-sounding, spacey, repetitive electronic tracks built around arpeggiated sequences and evolving synth layers.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient may be more textural or beatless; Berlin-School is often defined by pulsing sequencer patterns.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Age
distinguishFrom.difference: New Age is usually softer and relaxation-oriented; Berlin-School is more sequencer-driven and cosmic.

label: Electronic---Big Beat
description: Breakbeat-driven electronic music with large drums, rock attitude, heavy samples, and high-impact hooks.
classificationHint: Use this for loud, sample-heavy 1990s-style breakbeat tracks with aggressive drums and festival-sized energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakbeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakbeat is broader; Big Beat is usually bigger, rockier, and more sample-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trip Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Trip Hop is slower and moodier; Big Beat is more aggressive and party-oriented.

label: Electronic---Bleep
description: Early UK electronic dance style built from sparse bleeps, sub-bass, and minimal rhythmic patterns.
classificationHint: Use this for stripped, early-rave or techno-adjacent tracks where bleepy synth motifs and sub-bass dominate.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is broader and often more driving; Bleep is sparser and centered on bleep motifs and bass.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakbeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakbeat emphasizes broken drum patterns; Bleep is more defined by synth tone and sub-bass minimalism.

label: Electronic---Breakbeat
description: Electronic music built around broken drum patterns instead of a straight four-on-the-floor pulse.
classificationHint: Use this when the rhythm is clearly break-based and does not fit drum and bass, jungle, or big beat more specifically.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breaks
distinguishFrom.difference: Breaks is often a more club-specific breakbeat style; Breakbeat is the broader category.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass is much faster and more specific in bass and drum programming.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Big Beat
distinguishFrom.difference: Big Beat is usually more rock-like, sample-heavy, and hook-driven.

label: Electronic---Breakcore
description: An extreme electronic style using fast, heavily chopped breakbeats, distortion, and chaotic edits.
classificationHint: Use this for very fast, intense tracks with frantic drum slicing and abrasive, unstable structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass is usually more stable and groove-based; Breakcore is more chaotic and aggressively edited.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speedcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Speedcore is more kick-drum driven; Breakcore is more breakbeat and cut-up oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---J-Core
distinguishFrom.difference: J-Core can be fast and intense but is often more melodic or anime/game influenced.

label: Electronic---Breaks
description: Club-oriented breakbeat music with broken drum patterns, bass movement, and dancefloor structure.
classificationHint: Use this for breakbeat tracks that feel built for clubs but are not specifically drum and bass, jungle, or big beat.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakbeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakbeat is the wider rhythm category; Breaks is usually a more club-focused style.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive Breaks
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive Breaks has longer builds and more atmospheric progressive structure.

label: Electronic---Broken Beat
description: A syncopated electronic style with off-grid grooves, jazz-funk influence, and complex rhythmic movement.
classificationHint: Use this when the rhythm feels broken and sophisticated, often with soul, jazz, or future-funk influence.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Future Jazz
distinguishFrom.difference: Future Jazz emphasizes jazz atmosphere; Broken Beat emphasizes syncopated rhythm.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House usually has a steadier four-on-the-floor pulse.

label: Electronic---Chillwave
description: Lo-fi, nostalgic electronic pop with washed-out synths, soft vocals, and hazy retro atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this for dreamy, sun-faded electronic tracks with soft production, nostalgia, and relaxed tempo.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synthwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Synthwave is usually cleaner, more 1980s cinematic, and more driving; Chillwave is hazier and more lo-fi.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Vaporwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Vaporwave is often more sample-based, surreal, and slowed-down; Chillwave is closer to indie electronic pop.

label: Electronic---Chiptune
description: Electronic music using video-game-like chip sounds, 8-bit or 16-bit tones, and simple synthetic melodies.
classificationHint: Use this when the sound palette clearly resembles retro game consoles or tracker music.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Theme
distinguishFrom.difference: Theme refers to function in media; Chiptune refers to the sound palette.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synth-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Synth-pop uses broader pop synthesizer production, not necessarily game-chip timbres.

label: Electronic---Dance-pop
description: Pop music built for dancing, using electronic production, catchy vocals, and accessible club rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is song-oriented and vocal-driven, but the beat and production clearly aim at dancefloor energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electronic Pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Electronic Pop is defined by electronic production within pop songwriting; Dance-pop additionally requires a pronounced dancefloor-oriented beat and energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Europop
distinguishFrom.difference: Europop is a broader European pop category; Dance-pop is defined by dancefloor production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is usually more 1990s/2000s club-specific, faster, and more formulaic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House may be less song-oriented and less pop-vocal focused.

label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
description: Ambient music with ominous, bleak, industrial, ritual, or horror-like atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this for beatless or slow atmospheric tracks that feel threatening, cold, or disturbing rather than relaxing.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient can be neutral or calming; Dark Ambient is specifically ominous or unsettling.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drone
distinguishFrom.difference: Drone is defined by sustained tones; Dark Ambient is defined by mood and atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dungeon Synth
distinguishFrom.difference: Dungeon Synth often uses fantasy or medieval-sounding synth motifs; Dark Ambient is usually more abstract and cinematic.

label: Electronic---Darkwave
description: Dark, synth-based music connected to post-punk, gothic, and new wave aesthetics.
classificationHint: Use this when electronic textures combine with melancholic vocals, gothic mood, and cold wave-like atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Wave
distinguishFrom.difference: New Wave is broader and can be bright or poppy; Darkwave is colder and more gothic.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Goth Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: Goth Rock is more guitar-band oriented; Darkwave is more synth-centered.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Coldwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Coldwave is often starker and more minimal; Darkwave may be more lush or dramatic.

label: Electronic---Deep House
description: House music with warm chords, smooth bass, subtle vocals, and a deeper, more restrained club mood.
classificationHint: Use this for house tracks that feel warm, smooth, and atmospheric rather than aggressive or peak-time.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader; Deep House specifically emphasizes warmth, depth, and restraint.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tech House
distinguishFrom.difference: Tech House is usually more percussive and functional; Deep House is smoother and more chord-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Garage House
distinguishFrom.difference: Garage House is often more vocal, soulful, and swing-based.

label: Electronic---Deep Techno
description: Techno with atmospheric depth, subdued intensity, and hypnotic repetition.
classificationHint: Use this for techno tracks that feel spacious, deep, and immersive rather than hard, bright, or aggressively peak-time.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is broader; Deep Techno focuses on atmosphere and hypnotic depth.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dub Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Dub Techno usually has dub chords and echo-heavy stabs; Deep Techno may be less dub-influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Techno is more forceful and aggressive.

label: Electronic---Disco
description: Dance music with steady rhythm, groove-oriented bass, strings, funk influence, and a classic club feel.
classificationHint: Use this for electronic or dance tracks whose identity comes from disco groove and arrangement rather than house or synth-pop.

distinguishFrom.label: Funk / Soul---Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Funk / Soul Disco often sounds more live-band based; Electronic Disco may lean more into sequencers or electronic production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Nu-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Nu-Disco is a modern revival or reinterpretation of disco.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House usually has a more mechanical club beat and production structure.

label: Electronic---Disco Polo
description: A Polish dance-pop style with simple rhythms, bright synths, and direct singalong melodies.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a very accessible Polish dance-pop character with simple hooks and lightweight club production.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Schlager
distinguishFrom.difference: Schlager is broader German-language pop; Disco Polo is specifically Polish dance-pop.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is usually more club-oriented and internationally styled.

label: Electronic---Donk
description: A hard, bouncy UK dance style defined by a prominent metallic offbeat bass sound.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a fast, playful, hard dance rhythm and the characteristic donk bass is central.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up is more melodic and vocal-hook oriented; Donk is more defined by the bouncy donk bass sound.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard House
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard House is broader and often less playful or bass-stab focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Jumpstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Jumpstyle is more tied to a specific hard dance kick and jump rhythm.

label: Electronic---Doomcore
description: A dark, slow, heavy hardcore techno style with oppressive atmosphere and hard kicks.
classificationHint: Use this for very dark hardcore tracks that feel slow, heavy, and ominous rather than fast and euphoric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is broader and often faster; Doomcore is slower and much darker.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Gabber
distinguishFrom.difference: Gabber is usually faster and more aggressive; Doomcore is more oppressive and doom-laden.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Dark Ambient may be beatless; Doomcore keeps hardcore kick structure.

label: Electronic---Downtempo
description: Slow to mid-tempo electronic music focused on relaxed rhythm, atmosphere, and groove.
classificationHint: Use this for electronic tracks that are beat-based but not dancefloor-driven, often calm, warm, or introspective.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient may lack a clear beat; Downtempo usually keeps a rhythm or groove.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trip Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Trip Hop often has stronger hip-hop, dub, or smoky cinematic influence.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Chillwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Chillwave is more nostalgic and lo-fi pop-oriented.

label: Electronic---Drone
description: Minimal music built from sustained tones, slow changes, and dense texture rather than rhythm or melody.
classificationHint: Use this when long held sounds and gradual sonic movement are the main content of the track.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient can be atmospheric with more harmonic or textural variety; Drone is more static and sustained.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise is usually more abrasive; Drone can be smooth, heavy, or meditative.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Harsh Noise Wall
distinguishFrom.difference: Harsh Noise Wall is extreme, loud, and static noise; Drone is broader and may be tonal.

label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
description: Fast electronic music with rapid breakbeats, strong basslines, and high-energy rhythmic pressure.
classificationHint: Use this for tracks around 160-180 BPM with fast breaks and bass-focused structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Jungle
distinguishFrom.difference: Jungle usually has more chopped breakbeats, reggae/ragga influence, and older rave character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Halftime
distinguishFrom.difference: Halftime often shares DnB tempo but feels slower because of the half-time drum placement.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakcore is more chaotic and aggressively edited.

label: Electronic---Dub
description: Electronic or studio-based music using echo, reverb, bass focus, and stripped-down dub mixing techniques.
classificationHint: Use this when delay effects, bass space, and dub-style mixing are more important than conventional song structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Dub
distinguishFrom.difference: Reggae Dub is rooted more directly in reggae versions and rhythm sections; Electronic Dub may use dub technique in electronic production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dub Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Dub Techno applies dub chords and echoes inside a techno framework.

label: Electronic---Dub Techno
description: Techno built from deep chords, echo, reverb, and hypnotic repetition influenced by dub production.
classificationHint: Use this when techno structure is combined with spacious delay-heavy chords and a deep, submerged atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep Techno may be atmospheric without the specific dub chord and echo language.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Minimal Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Minimal Techno is more sparse and functional; Dub Techno is more echo-heavy and chordal.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dub
distinguishFrom.difference: Dub may not have a techno pulse or structure.

label: Electronic---Dubstep
description: Bass-heavy electronic music with sparse drums, sub-bass pressure, syncopation, and dark or aggressive sound design.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has dubstep-style half-time rhythm, wobble or heavy bass design, and strong low-end focus.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Grime
distinguishFrom.difference: Grime is more MC/vocal and UK rap oriented; Dubstep is more bass and instrumental drop focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass is much faster in drum feel; Dubstep usually has a half-time pulse.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Trap
distinguishFrom.difference: Trap is hip-hop-derived with 808s and triplet hats; Dubstep has different bass modulation and rhythm roots.

label: Electronic---Dungeon Synth
description: Atmospheric synth music with fantasy, medieval, dark ambient, or role-playing-game-like mood.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels like lo-fi fantasy soundtrack music, often with simple synth strings, choirs, or medieval motifs.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Dark Ambient is more abstract and ominous; Dungeon Synth often has fantasy or medieval melodic material.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Score
distinguishFrom.difference: Score refers to music composed for media; Dungeon Synth is a standalone style with fantasy aesthetics.

label: Electronic---EBM
description: Electronic Body Music: hard, mechanical electronic music with industrial influence, driving basslines, and commanding rhythms.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a strict, physical, industrial dance pulse with aggressive synth bass and often stern vocals.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Industrial
distinguishFrom.difference: Industrial is broader and may be non-dance or noisy; EBM is more body-music and dance-pulse oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Beat
distinguishFrom.difference: New Beat is slower and more club-groove oriented; EBM feels more militant and mechanical.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Darkwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Darkwave is more gothic and melodic; EBM is more rhythmic and forceful.

label: Electronic---Electro
description: Electronic music with machine-funk rhythm, synthetic bass, crisp drum machines, and a robotic feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has electro drum-machine patterns, syncopated bass, and a cold or robotic funk character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electro House
distinguishFrom.difference: Electro House is a later house style with bigger drops and four-on-the-floor structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Electro
distinguishFrom.difference: Hip Hop Electro is more directly tied to rap, breaking, and early hip-hop culture.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is usually more linear and less machine-funk syncopated.

label: Electronic---Electro House
description: House music with aggressive synth riffs, big drops, and a sharper, more compressed club sound.
classificationHint: Use this for house-tempo tracks with large electronic leads, punchy drops, and festival or club intensity.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and can be smoother; Electro House is more aggressive and drop-focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive House
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive House usually has longer melodic builds; Electro House is punchier and more riff-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is more song and vocal-hook oriented.

label: Electronic---Electroacoustic
description: Music combining electronic processing or synthesis with acoustic sounds, often in an experimental or art-music context.
classificationHint: Use this when acoustic sources and electronic manipulation are both central and the track feels more compositional than club-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Musique Concrète
distinguishFrom.difference: Musique Concrète is specifically based on recorded sound objects and tape/studio manipulation; Electroacoustic is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Classical---Contemporary
distinguishFrom.difference: Contemporary classical may include electroacoustic work, but this label emphasizes the electronic-acoustic method.

label: Electronic---Electroclash
description: A stylish electronic style combining electro, synth-pop, new wave, and punk-like attitude.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a cold retro-electro sound, fashion-conscious vocals, and a slightly ironic or edgy club-pop feel.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synth-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Synth-pop is more straightforward pop-song oriented; Electroclash is colder, edgier, and more club-fashion driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Wave
distinguishFrom.difference: New Wave is broader and often band-based; Electroclash is more explicitly electronic and club-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electro
distinguishFrom.difference: Electroclash adds vocal attitude and synth-pop/new-wave aesthetics to electro influence.

label: Electronic---Euro House
description: European house music with accessible hooks, bright production, and a direct club-pop feel.
classificationHint: Use this when house structure is present but the sound is clearly European, melodic, and commercially accessible.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader; Euro House is more European, pop-friendly, and hook-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is usually faster, more vocal-rap/sung hook based, and more 1990s dance-pop structured.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is more song-first and less specifically house-based.

label: Electronic---Euro-Disco
description: European disco style with polished synths, steady dance rhythm, and melodic pop structure.
classificationHint: Use this for disco-rooted tracks with a European synth-pop or Italo-like flavor.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Italo-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Italo-Disco is a more specific Italian-centered synth-disco sound.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is faster, more 1990s club-oriented, and usually more beat-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Funk / Soul---Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Funk / Soul Disco tends to sound more live-band and less synth-European.

label: Electronic---Eurobeat
description: Fast, high-energy European/Japanese dance style with bright synths, rapid tempo, and dramatic melodic hooks.
classificationHint: Use this for very energetic, fast dance tracks with driving rhythm, intense melody, and arcade/anime/racing-like momentum.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is usually slower and more club-pop oriented; Eurobeat is faster and more relentless.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Italodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Italodance is generally smoother and more Mediterranean club-pop; Eurobeat is faster and more intense.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up has a hard dance/trance bounce; Eurobeat is more racing-like and melodramatic.

label: Electronic---Eurodance
description: 1990s-style dance music with strong beats, catchy sung hooks, bright synths, and often rap verses.
classificationHint: Use this for accessible, high-energy club-pop tracks with clear verse/chorus structure and classic European dance production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up is usually faster, more trance-like, and more 2000s hard-dance oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is broader and more mainstream song-focused; Eurodance has a specific 1990s club formula.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurobeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurobeat is usually faster and more intense.

label: Electronic---Experimental
description: Electronic music that prioritizes unusual methods, structures, textures, or concepts over conventional genre rules.
classificationHint: Use this when the track resists standard classification and the unusual approach is its main identity.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Abstract
distinguishFrom.difference: Abstract often describes non-direct form or texture; Experimental emphasizes the method or boundary-pushing intent.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise is specifically abrasive or noise-centered; Experimental can be quiet, structured, or mixed-style.

label: Electronic---Footwork
description: Fast Chicago-rooted electronic dance music with syncopated percussion, chopped samples, and rhythms for footwork dancing.
classificationHint: Use this for around-160 BPM tracks with jittery drum programming, chopped vocal samples, and intense rhythmic movement.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Juke
distinguishFrom.difference: Juke is closely related and often broader or older; Footwork is more rhythmically complex and dance-battle oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass uses fast breaks and basslines; Footwork has a different Chicago rhythmic language.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Halftime
distinguishFrom.difference: Halftime often feels slower and bass-music oriented despite similar tempo ranges.

label: Electronic---Freestyle
description: Latin-influenced electronic dance-pop with syncopated drum machines, emotional vocals, and 1980s/1990s club feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track combines electro drum programming, pop vocals, and Latin club-pop sensibility.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electro
distinguishFrom.difference: Electro may be more robotic and instrumental; Freestyle is more vocal and pop-emotional.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is broader; Freestyle has a specific electro-Latin club-pop sound.

label: Electronic---Frenchcore
description: Fast, aggressive hardcore techno style with rolling distorted kicks, very high tempo, rave pressure, and often melodic or chaotic breakdowns.
classificationHint: Use this for fast hardcore tracks, usually around 170/180 BPM or higher, where rolling distorted kicks and frantic forward pressure dominate more than classic gabber roughness or hardstyle anthem structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is the broader parent category; Frenchcore is a more specific, faster, rolling-kick-driven hardcore style.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Gabber
distinguishFrom.difference: Gabber is usually rougher, more classic distorted-kick hardcore; Frenchcore is often faster, more rolling, and more frantic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardstyle is usually slower and more anthem-structured, with pitched kick melodies and dramatic breaks; Frenchcore is faster and more hardcore-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speedcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Speedcore is more extreme in tempo and often less melodic; Frenchcore stays closer to hardcore rave structure even when very fast.

label: Electronic---Future Jazz
description: Modern electronic music blending jazz harmony, live or sampled jazz elements, and club or downtempo production.
classificationHint: Use this when jazz texture is strong but the production feels electronic, modern, and groove-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Acid Jazz
distinguishFrom.difference: Acid Jazz is often funkier and more band-like; Future Jazz is usually more electronic and atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Jazz---Fusion
distinguishFrom.difference: Fusion is more jazz-band and instrumental-performance oriented.

label: Electronic---Gabber
description: Hardcore techno with distorted kicks, aggressive speed, and a raw rave sound.
classificationHint: Use this for very hard, fast electronic tracks where distorted kick drums dominate and the mood is aggressive rather than melodic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is broader; Gabber has a more specific distorted-kick, Dutch rave identity.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speedcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Speedcore is usually faster and more extreme.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Happy Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Happy Hardcore is more euphoric and melodic; Gabber is rougher and more aggressive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Frenchcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Frenchcore is usually faster and more rolling or melodic; Gabber is rougher, more classic Dutch hardcore, and more directly distorted-kick driven.

label: Electronic---Garage House
description: Soulful house music with strong vocals, swing, gospel or R&B influence, and warm club groove.
classificationHint: Use this for house tracks with soulful vocals, organ/chord warmth, and a swinging garage feel.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep House
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep House is smoother and more understated; Garage House is often more vocal and soulful.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and may not have the soulful garage character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---UK Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: UK Garage is usually more broken, swung, and bassline-oriented.

label: Electronic---Ghetto
description: Raw, stripped-down electronic club music with blunt rhythm, repetitive vocal samples, and street-level dance energy.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels deliberately minimal, rough, and vocal-sample driven in a ghetto club style.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ghetto House
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghetto House is specifically house-based; Ghetto can be used more broadly for raw club forms.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ghettotech
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghettotech is usually faster and more electro/bass influenced.

label: Electronic---Ghetto House
description: Raw Chicago house style with minimal drums, explicit or repetitive vocal samples, and direct club functionality.
classificationHint: Use this for stripped, repetitive house tracks with strong vocal chops and rough dancefloor energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and may be smoother or more musical; Ghetto House is rawer and more repetitive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Juke
distinguishFrom.difference: Juke is faster and more syncopated.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Baltimore Club
distinguishFrom.difference: Baltimore Club often uses chopped breaks and different regional rhythmic patterns.

label: Electronic---Ghettotech
description: Fast, raw electronic club music combining electro, techno, Miami bass, and ghetto house influence.
classificationHint: Use this for fast, rough club tracks with electro bass, repetitive vocals, and high-pressure rhythm.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ghetto House
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghetto House is usually slower and house-based; Ghettotech is faster and more electro/bass driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electro
distinguishFrom.difference: Electro is broader and may be less raw or vocal-sample driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Miami Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Miami Bass is more hip-hop/bass-party rooted; Ghettotech is more techno/electro club oriented.

label: Electronic---Glitch
description: Electronic music using digital errors, clicks, cuts, artifacts, and microscopic edits as musical material.
classificationHint: Use this when the sound design is built around clicks, skips, bit-crushing, edits, or malfunction-like textures.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---IDM
distinguishFrom.difference: IDM may use complex electronic rhythms but not necessarily glitch artifacts.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Experimental
distinguishFrom.difference: Experimental is broader; Glitch specifically uses digital artifact aesthetics.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Glitch Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Glitch Hop combines glitch textures with hip-hop-like groove.

label: Electronic---Glitch Hop
description: Hip-hop-tempo electronic music combining broken beats, bass weight, and glitchy edits or sound design.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a head-nod groove with glitch textures, chopped edits, and electronic bass design.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Glitch
distinguishFrom.difference: Glitch can be abstract or beatless; Glitch Hop has a clear hip-hop-style groove.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Instrumental
distinguishFrom.difference: Instrumental Hip Hop may be beat-based without glitch sound design.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dubstep
distinguishFrom.difference: Dubstep is usually around 140 BPM with half-time bass pressure; Glitch Hop is usually slower and funkier.

label: Electronic---Goa Trance
description: A psychedelic trance predecessor with hypnotic acid lines, Eastern-influenced melodies, and long energetic builds.
classificationHint: Use this for fast, swirling trance tracks with layered acid patterns and old-school psychedelic rave character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Psy-Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Psy-Trance is broader and often more modern, tighter, and bassline-focused; Goa Trance is more melodic and old-school.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Trance is broader and may be cleaner or more anthem-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Acid
distinguishFrom.difference: Acid describes the synth sound; Goa Trance is a full psychedelic trance style.

label: Electronic---Grime
description: UK electronic style tied to MC culture, sparse beats, dark synths, and around-140 BPM pressure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has grime rhythm, dark square-wave or icy synths, and a strong MC or instrumental grime identity.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Grime
distinguishFrom.difference: Hip Hop Grime emphasizes the rap/MC side; Electronic Grime may refer to instrumental or production style.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dubstep
distinguishFrom.difference: Dubstep is more bass/drop focused; Grime is more MC and sparse rhythm oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---UK Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: UK Garage is usually smoother and more swung; Grime is darker and harsher.

label: Electronic---Halftime
description: Bass music or drum-and-bass-adjacent style where high tempo is felt through slower, heavier half-time drum placement.
classificationHint: Use this when the track may be measured around 80–90 BPM or 160–180 BPM, but the groove lands with a slow, heavy half-time feel rather than full-speed Drum n Bass energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass usually feels fast in the drum movement; Halftime uses related tempo space but places the drums to feel slower and heavier.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dubstep
distinguishFrom.difference: Dubstep is usually centered around a 140 BPM half-time framework; Halftime is more DnB/bass-music adjacent.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Trap
distinguishFrom.difference: Trap uses hip-hop 808 patterns, triplet hats, and rap-derived structure; Halftime is more bass-music or Drum n Bass adjacent.

label: Electronic---Hands Up
description: Fast, melodic dance music with euphoric synth leads, clear kicks, and often catchy pitched or pop-style vocals.
classificationHint: Use this for bright, fast party-dance tracks with Eurodance, trance, or happy-hardcore flavor and an obvious hands-in-the-air hook.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is often older and more pop-rap structured; Hands Up is usually faster, more trance-like, and more 2000s hard-dance oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Happy Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Happy Hardcore is usually faster, more rave-like, and more hardcore-kick driven; Hands Up is smoother and more club-pop melodic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Trance is usually more trance-structure focused; Hands Up is more direct, vocal, and singalong-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Donk
distinguishFrom.difference: Donk is more defined by bouncy metallic bass; Hands Up is more defined by melody and euphoric leads.

label: Electronic---Happy Hardcore
description: Fast hardcore-rave music with cheerful melodies, bright synths, high energy, and often pitched-up vocals.
classificationHint: Use this for very fast, euphoric rave tracks where hardcore speed is combined with playful or uplifting melodic content.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is broader and can be darker or harsher; Happy Hardcore is specifically bright and euphoric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up is usually slower and smoother; Happy Hardcore is faster and more rave/hardcore driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---J-Core
distinguishFrom.difference: J-Core can share speed and melody but often has Japanese/anime/game culture cues.

label: Electronic---Hard Beat
description: A harder electronic dance style with forceful rhythm and club-oriented pressure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly hard and beat-driven but does not fit a more specific hard house, hard trance, techno, or hardcore label.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard House
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard House is more specific in bounce and club structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Techno is usually more linear and techno-focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is faster and more extreme.

label: Electronic---Hard House
description: Fast, energetic house-derived club music with tough kicks, bouncy bass, and high-intensity builds.
classificationHint: Use this for hard dance tracks with house structure, strong bounce, and peak-time club energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and usually less aggressive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Trance emphasizes trance melodies and long builds; Hard House is more bouncy and rhythm-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Donk
distinguishFrom.difference: Donk is a more specific bouncy UK style with a characteristic bass sound.

label: Electronic---Hard Techno
description: Techno with higher intensity, harder kicks, aggressive drive, and a dense peak-time feel.
classificationHint: Use this for forceful techno tracks that are harder and more relentless than standard techno but not hardcore.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is broader and can be minimal, deep, or moderate; Hard Techno is more aggressive and high-pressure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Schranz
distinguishFrom.difference: Schranz is usually even more distorted, loop-heavy, and abrasive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is usually faster, more distorted, and less techno-structured.

label: Electronic---Hard Trance
description: A harder form of trance with driving bass, strong kicks, and dramatic synth builds.
classificationHint: Use this when trance structure and melody are present but the sound is tougher, faster, and more forceful than regular trance.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Trance is broader and may be softer or more uplifting; Hard Trance is tougher and more driving.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up is more vocal-hook and party-dance oriented; Hard Trance is more trance-build focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard House
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard House is more bouncy and less trance-melodic.

label: Electronic---Hardcore
description: Fast, aggressive electronic dance music built around hard kicks, high intensity, and rave pressure.
classificationHint: Use this for hard electronic tracks that are faster and more extreme than hard techno or hardstyle but not clearly gabber, speedcore, or happy hardcore.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Gabber
distinguishFrom.difference: Gabber is a specific distorted-kick hardcore style; Hardcore is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardstyle is usually slower, more structured, and uses pitched distorted kicks with melodic breaks.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speedcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Speedcore is faster and more extreme.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Happy Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Happy Hardcore is more cheerful and euphoric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Frenchcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Frenchcore is a more specific hardcore style, usually faster, more rolling, and more frantic; Hardcore is the broader fallback label.

label: Electronic---Hardstyle
description: Hard dance music with distorted pitched kicks, reverse bass or raw kicks, dramatic breaks, and anthem-like melodies.
classificationHint: Use this for hard dance tracks around 150 BPM where the kick sound and big melodic or raw-dance structure are central.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is usually faster and less anthem-structured; Hardstyle is more controlled and kick-melody focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Jumpstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Jumpstyle is bouncier and more tied to jump dance rhythm; Hardstyle is heavier and more dramatic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Trance keeps a trance identity; Hardstyle is defined by distorted kicks and hard dance drops.

label: Electronic---Harsh Noise Wall
description: Extreme noise music built from dense, static walls of abrasive sound with little or no rhythmic change.
classificationHint: Use this only when the track is a near-continuous wall of harsh noise rather than structured electronic music.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise is broader and can be dynamic; Harsh Noise Wall is specifically static, dense, and extreme.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Power Electronics
distinguishFrom.difference: Power Electronics often includes confrontational vocals or industrial performance elements; Harsh Noise Wall is more static texture.

label: Electronic---Hi NRG
description: Fast, energetic disco and dance-pop style with driving bass, bright synths, and dramatic vocal hooks.
classificationHint: Use this for high-energy dance tracks with disco roots, strong pulse, and uplifting club-pop vocals.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Euro-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Euro-Disco is more European disco/synth-disco; Hi NRG is faster and more driving.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Italo-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Italo-Disco often has a cooler synth-pop feel; Hi NRG is more forceful and energetic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is later, more beat-driven, and often includes rap/sung structures.

label: Electronic---Hip Hop
description: Electronic production using hip-hop rhythms, sampling, drum machines, or rap-related structure within an electronic classification context.
classificationHint: Use this when the electronic track clearly borrows hip-hop beat language but is classified in the electronic style list.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Instrumental
distinguishFrom.difference: Hip Hop Instrumental is more directly part of hip-hop; Electronic Hip Hop may emphasize electronic production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Glitch Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Glitch Hop specifically adds glitch edits and electronic bass design.

label: Electronic---Hip-House
description: A hybrid of house music and hip-hop vocals or rap delivery.
classificationHint: Use this when a house beat is combined with rap vocals, hip-hop vocal phrasing, or early club-rap structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House may not include rap or hip-hop vocal delivery.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Pop Rap
distinguishFrom.difference: Pop Rap is hip-hop based; Hip-House is house-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is broader and more pop-song oriented.

label: Electronic---House
description: Four-on-the-floor electronic dance music with steady groove, repeating patterns, and club-oriented structure.
classificationHint: Use this as a broad house label when the track has house rhythm but no more specific house substyle clearly dominates.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep House
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep House is warmer and more atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tech House
distinguishFrom.difference: Tech House is more percussive and techno-influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Garage House
distinguishFrom.difference: Garage House is more soulful and vocal/swing oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electro House
distinguishFrom.difference: Electro House is more aggressive and drop-focused.

label: Electronic---IDM
description: Complex, cerebral electronic music with intricate rhythms, unusual sound design, and non-standard structure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is detailed and experimental but still musically structured, often with complex beats or abstract melody.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Glitch
distinguishFrom.difference: Glitch focuses on digital artifacts; IDM is broader and often more compositionally structured.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient is more atmospheric and less rhythmically complex.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Experimental
distinguishFrom.difference: Experimental is broader; IDM usually has a recognizable electronic music structure.

label: Electronic---Illbient
description: Dark, atmospheric, urban electronic music mixing ambient, dub, hip-hop, and experimental sound collage elements.
classificationHint: Use this for murky, downtempo, city-like soundscapes with dubby bass, samples, and uneasy atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trip Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Trip Hop is usually more song/groove based; Illbient is more abstract and urban-atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Dark Ambient may be beatless and more cinematic; Illbient often has dub or hip-hop rhythm traces.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Downtempo
distinguishFrom.difference: Downtempo is broader and usually less dark or experimental.

label: Electronic---Industrial
description: Electronic music using mechanical rhythms, harsh textures, noise elements, and a cold or confrontational atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when the sound is clearly machine-like, abrasive, or industrial rather than simply dark electronic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---EBM
distinguishFrom.difference: EBM is more dance-pulse and body-music oriented; Industrial is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise is more centered on abrasive sound itself; Industrial may include rhythm and song structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Industrial
distinguishFrom.difference: Rock Industrial is more band/guitar oriented.

label: Electronic---Italo House
description: Italian-influenced house music with warm piano chords, melodic hooks, and late-1980s/early-1990s club feel.
classificationHint: Use this when a house track has bright Italian club melody, piano riffs, and uplifting Mediterranean energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Euro House
distinguishFrom.difference: Euro House is broader; Italo House has a more specific Italian piano-house character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Garage House
distinguishFrom.difference: Garage House is more soulful and vocal/swing based.

label: Electronic---Italo-Disco
description: Synth-driven European disco style associated with Italian production, catchy melodies, and drum-machine rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this for melodic synth-disco tracks with cool vocals, arpeggiated basslines, and 1980s European character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Euro-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Euro-Disco is broader; Italo-Disco is more specific in synth sound and Italian/European 1980s character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synth-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Synth-pop is more song-pop oriented; Italo-Disco is more dance/disco oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hi NRG
distinguishFrom.difference: Hi NRG is usually faster and more forceful.

label: Electronic---Italodance
description: Melodic Italian dance music with bright synth leads, accessible vocals, and smooth club rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this for 1990s/2000s-style Italian dance tracks that are melodic, catchy, and less hard than Hands Up or Hardstyle.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurodance
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurodance is broader and often more formulaic with rap/sung hooks; Italodance has a smoother Italian melodic club sound.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up is usually harder, faster, and more euphoric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Eurobeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Eurobeat is faster and more intense.

label: Electronic---J-Core
description: Japanese hardcore and hard dance style often mixing speed, bright melodies, game/anime aesthetics, and intense kicks.
classificationHint: Use this when fast hardcore or hard dance sound is combined with distinctly Japanese, anime, game, or otaku-culture cues.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Happy Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Happy Hardcore is bright and fast but not necessarily Japanese/anime influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speedcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Speedcore is more extreme and less necessarily melodic or Japanese-styled.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is broader and may lack the melodic/anime/game flavor.

label: Electronic---Jazzdance
description: Dance-oriented music blending jazz elements with club rhythm and accessible groove.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels made for dancing but uses jazz phrasing, instrumentation, or harmony as a central feature.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Future Jazz
distinguishFrom.difference: Future Jazz is more electronic and atmospheric; Jazzdance is more directly danceable.

distinguishFrom.label: Jazz---Jazz-Funk
distinguishFrom.difference: Jazz-Funk is more band/groove oriented and less electronic-club focused.

label: Electronic---Juke
description: Fast Chicago club music with repetitive vocal samples, syncopated rhythms, and raw dance energy.
classificationHint: Use this for fast, minimal, footwork-adjacent tracks with chopped vocals and sharp rhythmic drive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Footwork
distinguishFrom.difference: Footwork is usually more rhythmically complex and dance-battle oriented; Juke can be rawer and more direct.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ghetto House
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghetto House is usually slower and more house-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ghettotech
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghettotech is more electro/bass and techno influenced.

label: Electronic---Jumpstyle
description: Hard dance style with a bouncy kick rhythm, simple hard melodies, and a structure suited to jump dance.
classificationHint: Use this for hard dance tracks with a clear jump rhythm and bouncy, repetitive momentum.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardstyle is heavier and more dramatic, with more developed kick design and breaks.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Donk
distinguishFrom.difference: Donk is defined by a metallic bass sound; Jumpstyle is defined more by jump rhythm and hard dance structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard House
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard House is broader and more house-derived.

label: Electronic---Jungle
description: Fast breakbeat music with chopped Amen-style breaks, deep bass, reggae/ragga influence, and rave energy.
classificationHint: Use this for fast tracks with complex chopped breaks, sub-bass, and old-school breakbeat/rave character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass is usually cleaner, more modern, and more bassline-programmed; Jungle is breakier and often more reggae/ragga influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakbeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakbeat is slower and broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakcore is more chaotic and extreme.

label: Electronic---Latin
description: Electronic dance music using Latin rhythms, percussion, melodies, or vocal style.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is primarily electronic but its rhythmic or melodic identity clearly comes from Latin music.

distinguishFrom.label: Latin---Reggaeton
distinguishFrom.difference: Reggaeton is a specific Latin genre with dembow rhythm; Electronic Latin is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Latin---Salsa
distinguishFrom.difference: Salsa is a band-based Latin dance style; Electronic Latin only borrows Latin elements inside electronic production.

label: Electronic---Leftfield
description: Unconventional electronic music that sits outside mainstream club and pop structures while remaining accessible enough to be genre-adjacent.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly electronic but unusual, off-center, or hard to place without being purely experimental or noise.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Experimental
distinguishFrom.difference: Experimental is more explicitly boundary-pushing; Leftfield can be unusual but still groove- or song-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---IDM
distinguishFrom.difference: IDM often has complex programming; Leftfield is broader and more about being outside the norm.

label: Electronic---Lento Violento
description: Slow, heavy Italian electronic style with pounding kicks, dark bass, and deliberate hard-dance weight.
classificationHint: Use this for slow but heavy tracks with a hard electronic pulse and an Italian hard-dance character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardstyle is faster and more anthem-like; Lento Violento is slower and heavier.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Doomcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Doomcore is darker and hardcore-rooted; Lento Violento is more Italian hard-dance oriented.

label: Electronic---Makina
description: Fast Spanish rave-oriented electronic music with driving kicks, rapid basslines, and bright melodic synth patterns.
classificationHint: Use this for very fast rave tracks that sit near happy hardcore, hard trance, and early hardcore, especially when the rhythm feels direct and high-pressure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Happy Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Happy Hardcore is usually more openly euphoric, vocal-driven, and playful; Makina often feels more direct, mechanical, and rave-focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Trance usually has longer trance-style builds and a cleaner club structure; Makina is often faster, more compact, and more bassline-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is broader and often harsher; Makina keeps a more melodic Spanish rave identity.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Gabber
distinguishFrom.difference: Gabber is usually more distorted and aggressive; Makina is typically more melodic and less kick-abrasive.

label: Electronic---Minimal
description: Electronic music based on sparse elements, repetition, subtle changes, and reduced arrangement.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is defined by economy of elements and gradual development rather than melody, vocals, or big drops.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Minimal Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Minimal Techno is specifically techno-based; Minimal can apply more broadly.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep House
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep House is warmer and more chordal; Minimal is more reduced and sparse.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---IDM
distinguishFrom.difference: IDM is often more complex; Minimal is deliberately reduced.

label: Electronic---Minimal Techno
description: Techno built from sparse percussion, small changes, repetition, and functional club structure.
classificationHint: Use this for reduced techno tracks where subtle rhythmic and textural changes are the main movement.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is broader; Minimal Techno is more stripped down and repetitive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dub Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Dub Techno is echo-heavy and chordal; Minimal Techno is more dry and reduced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Minimal
distinguishFrom.difference: Minimal is broader and not necessarily techno-based.

label: Electronic---Modern Classical
description: Contemporary classical-influenced music using modern composition, electronic production, or cinematic minimalism.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has classical instrumentation or composition but feels modern, ambient, or electronically produced.

distinguishFrom.label: Classical---Contemporary
distinguishFrom.difference: Contemporary Classical is more directly part of the classical tradition; Modern Classical here often overlaps with ambient, cinematic, or electronic production.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Score
distinguishFrom.difference: Score refers to media function; Modern Classical refers to musical language.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
