distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient is more texture-focused; Modern Classical relies more on classical harmony or instrumentation.

label: Electronic---Musique Concrète
description: Experimental music made from recorded sounds, edited audio objects, and studio manipulation rather than conventional instruments.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is built from manipulated real-world recordings or sound objects in an art-music context.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Sound Collage
distinguishFrom.difference: Sound Collage may combine many sources freely; Musique Concrète has a stronger historical art-music and recorded-sound focus.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electroacoustic
distinguishFrom.difference: Electroacoustic is broader and may combine instruments with electronics.

distinguishFrom.label: Non-Music---Field Recording
distinguishFrom.difference: Field Recording documents real-world sound; Musique Concrète transforms recordings into composition.

label: Electronic---Neo Trance
description: Modern trance-influenced electronic music with smoother textures, restrained euphoria, and often house or techno influence.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has trance-like melody and atmosphere but avoids classic big-room or old-school trance formulas.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Trance is broader and often more direct or anthemic; Neo Trance is more modern and restrained.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive House
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive House is more house-groove based; Neo Trance retains a stronger trance atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive Trance is usually more explicitly trance-structured and build-oriented.

label: Electronic---Neofolk
description: Dark, often acoustic or ritual-influenced music with folk instrumentation and post-industrial atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this only when the electronic classification points to dark folk/industrial crossover rather than normal folk music.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Neofolk
distinguishFrom.difference: Rock Neofolk is more likely guitar/song based; Electronic Neofolk may be more ambient, ritual, or industrial-adjacent.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Folk
distinguishFrom.difference: Folk is broader and usually less dark or post-industrial.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Dark Ambient is more textural and less song/folk based.

label: Electronic---New Age
description: Soft, atmospheric music associated with relaxation, meditation, spirituality, or gentle instrumental mood.
classificationHint: Use this for calm, smooth, spacious tracks intended to feel soothing or reflective rather than club-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Ambient can be abstract or neutral; New Age is usually more relaxing, spiritual, or wellness-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Modern Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Modern Classical has stronger classical composition or instrumentation.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drone
distinguishFrom.difference: Drone is more sustained and minimal.

label: Electronic---New Beat
description: Slow, heavy Belgian club style with dark synths, EBM influence, and deliberate mid-tempo groove.
classificationHint: Use this for dark, slower electronic dance tracks with heavy groove and late-1980s club character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---EBM
distinguishFrom.difference: EBM is usually more forceful and mechanical; New Beat is slower and more club-groove oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Acid House
distinguishFrom.difference: Acid House is more house and acid-bass focused; New Beat is darker and slower.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Darkwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Darkwave is more song/gothic oriented; New Beat is more club rhythm oriented.

label: Electronic---New Wave
description: Synth and post-punk-influenced music with pop structure, electronic textures, and late-1970s/1980s character.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a new-wave blend of pop songwriting, synths, and band or electronic elements.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---New Wave
distinguishFrom.difference: Rock New Wave is more band/guitar oriented; Electronic New Wave emphasizes synth/electronic production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synth-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Synth-pop is more fully synth-driven and pop-melodic; New Wave can include more post-punk or band elements.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Darkwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Darkwave is darker and more gothic.

label: Electronic---Noise
description: Music or sound art using abrasive, distorted, chaotic, or non-pitched sound as a primary material.
classificationHint: Use this when noise texture itself is the main content, not just a harsh layer inside another genre.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Harsh Noise Wall
distinguishFrom.difference: Harsh Noise Wall is a specific static, dense form of noise.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Power Electronics
distinguishFrom.difference: Power Electronics is more confrontational and often vocal/performance based.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Rock Noise often comes from guitars or band performance.

label: Electronic---Nu-Disco
description: Modern disco-influenced dance music with clean production, funk bass, and contemporary club structure.
classificationHint: Use this for modern electronic tracks that revive disco groove with polished club production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Disco may refer to original or classic disco; Nu-Disco is modern and reinterpretive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and more beat-structure focused; Nu-Disco keeps disco groove and feel.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synthwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Synthwave is more 1980s cinematic and retro-synth; Nu-Disco is more funk/disco groove based.

label: Electronic---Power Electronics
description: Extreme industrial/noise music with harsh electronics, confrontational intensity, and often screamed or provocative vocals.
classificationHint: Use this only for abrasive, aggressive, industrial-noise material where confrontation is central.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise is broader and may be abstract; Power Electronics is more confrontational and performance-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Harsh Noise Wall
distinguishFrom.difference: Harsh Noise Wall is more static and texture-focused; Power Electronics often has vocal or thematic aggression.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Industrial
distinguishFrom.difference: Industrial is broader and may be rhythmic or song-based.

label: Electronic---Progressive Breaks
description: Breakbeat music with progressive structure, long builds, atmospheric layers, and melodic development.
classificationHint: Use this for club-oriented breaks that unfold gradually like progressive house or trance.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breaks
distinguishFrom.difference: Breaks is broader and may be more direct; Progressive Breaks has longer builds and a more atmospheric arc.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive House
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive House uses a steadier four-on-the-floor groove; Progressive Breaks uses broken beats.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive Trance has a stronger trance pulse and melody language.

label: Electronic---Progressive House
description: House music with gradual builds, layered melodies, atmospheric development, and smooth club structure.
classificationHint: Use this for house-tempo tracks that evolve over time with melodic or atmospheric progression rather than simple loops.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and may be more loop-based; Progressive House emphasizes gradual development.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electro House
distinguishFrom.difference: Electro House is punchier and drop-focused; Progressive House is smoother and more layered.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tech House
distinguishFrom.difference: Tech House is more percussive and functional; Progressive House is more melodic and expansive.

label: Electronic---Progressive Trance
description: Trance with gradual development, atmospheric layers, and restrained melodic builds.
classificationHint: Use this for trance tracks that evolve smoothly and progressively instead of relying on immediate anthem hooks.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Trance is broader and may be more anthem-like; Progressive Trance is more gradual and atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive House
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive House has a house groove; Progressive Trance has stronger trance pulse and synth language.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Neo Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Neo Trance is usually more modern and restrained, often house/techno-adjacent.

label: Electronic---Psy-Trance
description: Psychedelic trance with fast rolling basslines, layered synth effects, and hypnotic high-energy structure.
classificationHint: Use this for fast trance tracks with psychedelic sound design, driving bass, and long hypnotic progression.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Goa Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Goa Trance is often more old-school, melodic, and acid-layered; Psy-Trance can be tighter, darker, and more modern.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Trance is broader and may be less psychedelic or bassline-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive Trance is usually smoother and less intense.

label: Electronic---Rhythmic Noise
description: Noise-influenced electronic music with harsh textures organized around strong repetitive rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this when industrial or noise sound design is harsh, but the track has a clear driving rhythmic framework.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise can be non-rhythmic; Rhythmic Noise has an obvious beat or pulse.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Industrial
distinguishFrom.difference: Industrial is broader and may be song-based; Rhythmic Noise emphasizes abrasive rhythm.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Power Electronics
distinguishFrom.difference: Power Electronics is more confrontational and less necessarily dance-rhythmic.

label: Electronic---Schranz
description: Very hard, loop-heavy techno with distorted percussion, relentless drive, and abrasive peak-time energy.
classificationHint: Use this for hard techno that is especially pounding, compressed, repetitive, and aggressive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Techno is broader; Schranz is more distorted, loop-heavy, and extreme.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno is much broader and often less aggressive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is faster and kick-distortion focused; Schranz remains techno-structured.

label: Electronic---Sound Collage
description: Music or sound art assembled from many audio fragments, samples, recordings, and abrupt juxtapositions.
classificationHint: Use this when the composition feels like an arranged collage of sound sources rather than a conventional track.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Musique Concrète
distinguishFrom.difference: Musique Concrète has a stronger historical art-music focus on recorded sound objects; Sound Collage is broader and may be sample-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Cut-up/DJ
distinguishFrom.difference: Cut-up/DJ is more DJ or hip-hop technique oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Experimental
distinguishFrom.difference: Experimental is broader and not necessarily collage-based.

label: Electronic---Speed Garage
description: UK garage-related style with swung drums, bass pressure, vocal chops, and a faster, darker club feel.
classificationHint: Use this for garage tracks with strong swing, heavy bass, and energetic late-1990s UK club character.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---UK Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: UK Garage is broader and can be smoother; Speed Garage is more bass-heavy and driving.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Bassline
distinguishFrom.difference: Bassline often has more prominent bass hooks and a later UK club feel.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Garage House
distinguishFrom.difference: Garage House is more house and soulful vocal oriented.

label: Electronic---Speedcore
description: Extremely fast hardcore techno with very high BPM, distorted kicks, and maximal intensity.
classificationHint: Use this for hardcore tracks whose speed and aggression go beyond normal hardcore or gabber.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is broader and usually slower; Speedcore is defined by extreme tempo.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Gabber
distinguishFrom.difference: Gabber is aggressive but usually less extremely fast.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Breakcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Breakcore often uses chopped breaks; Speedcore is more kick-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Frenchcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Frenchcore can be very fast but usually stays closer to hardcore rave structure; Speedcore is defined by more extreme tempo and aggression.

label: Electronic---Synth-pop
description: Pop music built around synthesizers, drum machines, melodic vocals, and electronic arrangement.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly pop-song oriented but the main instrumentation and identity are synth-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Electronic Pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Electronic Pop is the broader category for pop shaped by electronic production; Synth-pop specifically makes synthesizers and programmed instrumentation its stylistic identity.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Wave
distinguishFrom.difference: New Wave may include more band/post-punk elements; Synth-pop is more fully synth-driven and pop-melodic.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Vocal
distinguishFrom.difference: Vocal pop is broader and may not be electronic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Italo-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Italo-Disco is more dance/disco oriented; Synth-pop is more song-pop oriented.

label: Electronic---Synthwave
description: Retro-futuristic electronic music inspired by 1980s synths, film scores, arcade imagery, and driving neon atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this for electronic tracks with clear 1980s-style synth palette, cinematic retro mood, and often steady mid-tempo drive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Chillwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Chillwave is hazier, lo-fi, and indie-pop leaning; Synthwave is cleaner, more cinematic, and more 1980s action/night-drive oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Vaporwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Vaporwave is more sample-based, slowed, and surreal; Synthwave is more composed and driving.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Italo-Disco
distinguishFrom.difference: Italo-Disco is dance/disco-song oriented; Synthwave is more cinematic retro-electronic.

label: Electronic---Tech House
description: House music with techno-influenced percussion, stripped grooves, and functional club structure.
classificationHint: Use this for house-tempo tracks where groove and percussion dominate more than vocals, chords, or big melodies.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader; Tech House is more percussive and techno-influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep House
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep House is warmer and more chordal; Tech House is drier and more functional.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Minimal Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Minimal Techno is more reduced and techno-based; Tech House keeps house groove.

label: Electronic---Tech Trance
description: Trance combining driving techno percussion with trance builds, basslines, and synth tension.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has trance structure but a harder, more technical, techno-like rhythm section.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Trance is broader and often more melodic; Tech Trance is tighter, harder, and more percussion-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Trance is more openly hard-dance and melodic; Tech Trance is more techno-percussive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Techno usually lacks the trance build and release structure.

label: Electronic---Techno
description: Repetitive electronic dance music built around machine rhythm, steady pulse, and gradual textural or rhythmic development.
classificationHint: Use this as the broad techno label when the track has a driving electronic pulse but no more specific techno substyle dominates.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House usually has a warmer groove and more swing or chord-vocal identity; Techno is more machine-like and linear.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Techno is more aggressive and high-pressure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Minimal Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Minimal Techno is more sparse and reduced.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep Techno
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep Techno is more atmospheric and immersive.

label: Electronic---Trance
description: Melodic electronic dance music with hypnotic repetition, builds, breakdowns, and uplifting or emotional synth themes.
classificationHint: Use this as the broad trance label when the track has trance structure and melodic drive but no more specific trance substyle dominates.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Progressive Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Progressive Trance is more gradual and atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hard Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Trance is tougher and more driving.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Goa Trance
distinguishFrom.difference: Goa Trance is more psychedelic, acid-layered, and old-school.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hands Up
distinguishFrom.difference: Hands Up is more direct, vocal, and party-dance oriented.

label: Electronic---Tribal
description: Electronic music using tribal-style percussion, chants, or ritual-like rhythmic patterns.
classificationHint: Use this when the main identity is percussion-heavy and tribal-coded rather than a specific house or techno substyle.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tribal House
distinguishFrom.difference: Tribal House is specifically house-based; Tribal is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---African
distinguishFrom.difference: African refers to regional/cultural music; Tribal in electronic contexts often means percussion style rather than authentic tradition.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Downtempo
distinguishFrom.difference: Downtempo may be slow and atmospheric without tribal percussion emphasis.

label: Electronic---Tribal House
description: House music centered on heavy percussion, tribal drum patterns, chants, and extended groove.
classificationHint: Use this for house-tempo tracks where layered percussion and tribal-style rhythm are the defining features.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and may rely on chords or vocals; Tribal House is percussion-dominant.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tribal
distinguishFrom.difference: Tribal is broader and not necessarily house-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tech House
distinguishFrom.difference: Tech House is more dry and techno-percussive; Tribal House has more hand-drum or chant-like feel.

label: Electronic---Trip Hop
description: Slow, moody electronic music mixing hip-hop beats, dub bass, samples, and cinematic atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this for downtempo tracks with smoky, dark, sample-based groove and hip-hop-influenced drums.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Downtempo
distinguishFrom.difference: Downtempo is broader and can be lighter; Trip Hop is moodier, more sample/dub/hip-hop influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Trip Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Hip Hop Trip Hop emphasizes the hip-hop side; Electronic Trip Hop may emphasize production atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Illbient
distinguishFrom.difference: Illbient is more abstract, urban, and experimental.

label: Electronic---Tropical House
description: Soft, melodic house-pop with warm chords, relaxed tempo, and tropical-flavored synth or percussion sounds.
classificationHint: Use this for accessible, sunny house tracks with relaxed pop vocals and light tropical atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Deep House
distinguishFrom.difference: Deep House is usually deeper and more club-oriented; Tropical House is lighter, poppier, and sunnier.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is broader and may not use house groove or tropical sound palette.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and usually less specifically tropical or pop-relaxed.

label: Electronic---UK Funky
description: UK club style combining house tempo with syncopated drums, Afro-Caribbean rhythms, and bass-driven groove.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has UK club rhythm, funky percussion, and house/bass structure with Afro-Caribbean movement.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---UK Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: UK Garage has more swing and garage vocal/bass language; UK Funky has more percussive Afro-Caribbean rhythmic movement.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---House
distinguishFrom.difference: House is broader and usually less syncopated/percussive.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Tribal House
distinguishFrom.difference: Tribal House is percussion-heavy but less specifically UK club oriented.

label: Electronic---UK Garage
description: UK club style with swung rhythms, chopped vocals, syncopated drums, and bassline movement.
classificationHint: Use this for garage tracks with clear swing, vocal chops, and a UK club feel, especially around 130 BPM.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speed Garage
distinguishFrom.difference: Speed Garage is heavier and more bass-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Bassline
distinguishFrom.difference: Bassline is more centered on prominent bass hooks.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Garage House
distinguishFrom.difference: Garage House is smoother, more soulful, and house-based.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Grime
distinguishFrom.difference: Grime is darker, sparser, and more MC-oriented.

label: Electronic---Vaporwave
description: Surreal, nostalgic electronic music often using slowed samples, retro corporate/media aesthetics, and hazy digital atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels like slowed, dreamlike, retro-media collage or synthetic nostalgia rather than standard synth-pop or ambient.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Chillwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Chillwave is more indie-pop and song-like; Vaporwave is more sample-based, surreal, and conceptually nostalgic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synthwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Synthwave is more composed, driving, and cinematic; Vaporwave is often slower and more surreal.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Sound Collage
distinguishFrom.difference: Sound Collage is broader and not necessarily tied to vaporwave aesthetics.

label: Electronic---Witch House
description: Dark, occult-leaning electronic music with slowed beats, ghostly vocals, heavy synths, and hazy atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this for dark, slow electronic tracks with occult, gothic, or haunted pop/bass-music aesthetics.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Darkwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Darkwave is more gothic song/synth based; Witch House is more slowed, hazy, and bass/electronic oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Trip Hop
distinguishFrom.difference: Trip Hop is smoky and sample/hip-hop influenced; Witch House is more occult and synthetic.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dark Ambient
distinguishFrom.difference: Dark Ambient is usually less beat or vocal oriented.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Aboriginal
description: A broad catalog label for the diverse music traditions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples of Australia, including ceremonial song, clan-specific vocal practices, didjeridu traditions, and contemporary Indigenous popular music.
classificationHint: Use only with documented Australian Indigenous cultural or artist context; it is not one unified sound, and didjeridu presence alone is insufficient.

label: Folk, World, & Country---African
description: A continental umbrella covering thousands of distinct African community, court, devotional, art, and popular music traditions rather than a single genre, rhythm, instrumentation, or production style.
classificationHint: Use only when African provenance is known but no regional or stylistic label can be assigned; prefer a specific tradition such as Highlife, Mbalax, Soukous, Griot repertory, or Maloya whenever evidence permits.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Andalusian Classical
description: A family of North African urban art-music traditions preserving and reshaping the medieval Andalusi legacy through modal suites such as the nūba, performed by voices with oud, bowed strings, qanun, winds, and percussion.
classificationHint: Use for documented Maghrebi Andalusi art music organized in modal suite form; the name does not mean Spanish flamenco or generic music from modern Andalusia.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Flamenco
distinguishFrom.difference: Andalusian Classical is a Maghrebi modal art-music tradition; Flamenco is a distinct southern Spanish cante, baile, and guitar practice.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Ottoman Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Both are modal court/urban traditions, but Andalusian Classical belongs to North African nūba lineages and Ottoman Classical to the Ottoman makam system.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Andean Music
description: A broad family of Indigenous, mestizo, rural, and urban traditions from the Andes, encompassing many ritual, work, dance, and song forms and instruments such as siku, quena, charango, harp, violin, brass, and regional drums.
classificationHint: Use when documented Andean regional context and repertory are clear but no narrower form fits; panpipes, charango, or Quechua language alone do not make every track the same Andean genre.

distinguishFrom.label: Latin---Quechua
distinguishFrom.difference: Andean Music is a geographic musical umbrella; Quechua is a language and cultural umbrella that overlaps but is not identical.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Appalachian Music
description: A regional music family of the Appalachian Mountains shaped by British and Irish ballads, African American banjo and blues traditions, sacred singing, fiddle tunes, and community dance music.
classificationHint: Use for historically rooted Appalachian ballad, fiddle-banjo, string-band, or vocal practice; Bluegrass is a later professional style with arranged breaks and a standardized ensemble.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Bluegrass
distinguishFrom.difference: Appalachian music is a broad regional tradition; Bluegrass is a later, tightly arranged professional string-band style.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Hillbilly
distinguishFrom.difference: Appalachian identifies regional tradition; Hillbilly is a historical record-industry umbrella covering several rural southern styles.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Basque Music
description: A cultural umbrella for traditional and modern music of the Basque Country, including unaccompanied song, bertsolaritza improvised verse, trikitixa accordion dance music, txalaparta percussion, pipes, choirs, and contemporary hybrids.
classificationHint: Use only with Basque language, regional instruments, repertory, or documented artist context; it is not a single rhythm and should not be inferred from accordion or folk-rock sound alone.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Bhangra
description: A Punjabi dance-music tradition derived from harvest celebration, marked by powerful dhol rhythms, boliyān vocal calls, tumbi or chimta figures, and energetic dance; modern Bhangra often adds bass, synthesizers, hip-hop, and electronic production.
classificationHint: Use when Punjabi dhol patterns, vocal language, and Bhangra dance phrasing are central; a generic South Asian pop track with electronic drums is not sufficient.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Bluegrass
description: A postwar American acoustic string-band style built on five-string banjo, mandolin, fiddle, guitar, and bass, with rapid precision, alternating instrumental breaks, close harmony, and the high-lonesome vocal sound.
classificationHint: Use when the standardized acoustic ensemble, driving off-beat rhythm, and passed solo breaks define the performance; older communal fiddle music belongs under Appalachian or Folk.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Appalachian Music
distinguishFrom.difference: Bluegrass uses a standardized postwar ensemble and alternating solos; Appalachian music is the broader regional source tradition.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Country
distinguishFrom.difference: Bluegrass is acoustic, break-driven string-band music; Country covers a much wider commercial field and may use drums, electric instruments, and pop production.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Cajun
description: French-language social dance music of Louisiana Cajun communities, rooted in Acadian ballads and fiddle tunes and commonly featuring diatonic accordion, fiddle, guitar, triangle, and forceful high-register vocals.
classificationHint: Use when Cajun French repertory, fiddle-accordion interplay, and two-step or waltz dance forms are central; Zydeco is the related Black Creole tradition with stronger blues and R&B rhythm.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Zydeco
distinguishFrom.difference: Cajun centers Acadian French fiddle-and-accordion repertory; Zydeco is a Black Creole style with rubboard and stronger blues/R&B drive.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Canzone Napoletana
description: The urban song tradition of Naples, especially the composed repertory popularized from the nineteenth century onward, marked by Neapolitan-language lyrics, expansive melody, theatrical vocal expression, and mandolin, guitar, piano, or orchestral accompaniment.
classificationHint: Use for documented Neapolitan song repertory or convincing Neapolitan vocal style; generic Italian pop, opera aria, and other regional folk song should not receive the label.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Carnatic
description: The classical music tradition of South India, organized through rāga and tāla and emphasizing composed kriti repertory, ornamented vocal or instrumental melody, and improvisatory sections with violin, mridangam, tambura, vina, flute, or related instruments.
classificationHint: Use for documented South Indian classical performance and Carnatic rāga-tāla grammar; Hindustani is the distinct northern tradition, and Indian Classical is the umbrella when the branch is uncertain.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Hindustani
distinguishFrom.difference: Carnatic is the South Indian classical system with its own repertory, ornament, and concert form; Hindustani is the North Indian tradition.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Indian Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Carnatic is one specific branch of the broader Indian Classical category.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Catalan Music
description: A broad cultural label for music rooted in Catalan-speaking regions, from traditional song, sardana dance and cobla wind ensembles to Nova Cançó and contemporary regional styles.
classificationHint: Use when Catalan language, sardana/cobla practice, regional repertory, or documented Catalan identity is central; it is not a single sonic genre.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Basque Music
distinguishFrom.difference: Catalan Music and Basque Music refer to different linguistic and regional traditions; neither can be identified by generic Iberian folk instrumentation alone.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Celtic
description: A broad modern umbrella for traditional and revival music associated with Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Brittany, Cornwall, and related diasporas, often drawing on reels, jigs, ballads, pipes, fiddles, harps, and regional languages.
classificationHint: Use when a specific Celtic-region repertory or a deliberate pan-Celtic revival style is evident; fiddle, whistle, drones, or fantasy atmosphere alone do not establish the category.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Nordic
distinguishFrom.difference: Celtic refers to Atlantic Celtic-region traditions; Nordic refers to Scandinavian and North Atlantic traditions with different repertories and dance forms.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Chacarera
description: An Argentine folk song and partner dance associated especially with Santiago del Estero, using a lively interplay of 6/8 and 3/4 accents, repeated dance sections, guitar, bombo legüero, violin, and sung coplas.
classificationHint: Use when the characteristic chacarera rhythmic cycle and Argentine dance form are identifiable; Tango is an urban Río de la Plata tradition with different meter, phrasing, and ensemble language.

distinguishFrom.label: Latin---Tango
distinguishFrom.difference: Chacarera is a rural Argentine folk dance with cross-accented 6/8–3/4 rhythm; Tango is an urban Río de la Plata form usually in duple or quadruple meter.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Chinese Classical
description: A broad catalog label for Chinese art-music traditions, including solo qin and pipa repertories, silk-and-bamboo ensembles, court and literati music, and regional instrumental forms with distinct modal, timbral, and notational practices.
classificationHint: Use only with documented Chinese art-music repertory or performance tradition; traditional instruments alone do not distinguish classical, folk, opera, ceremonial, or modern composition.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Chutney
description: An Indo-Caribbean popular dance style developed especially in Trinidad, Tobago, Guyana, and Suriname, joining Bhojpuri-derived wedding and folk songs with dholak, dhantal, harmonium, calypso, soca, and later electronic production.
classificationHint: Use when Indo-Caribbean vocals and rhythmic/instrumental vocabulary are combined with Caribbean dance music; Indian filmi-pop or Soca without this cultural synthesis should keep its own label.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Soca
distinguishFrom.difference: Chutney combines Indo-Caribbean song and instruments with Caribbean rhythm; Soca does not require that South Asian foundation.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Copla
description: A Spanish theatrical popular-song form, especially associated with twentieth-century Andalusia, built around dramatic narrative lyrics, strongly projected vocals, and orchestrated canción española arrangements.
classificationHint: Use when the staged, narrative Spanish song and declamatory vocal style dominate; Flamenco is organized around cante, toque, compás, and palos rather than orchestral popular song.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Flamenco
distinguishFrom.difference: Copla is an orchestrated theatrical song tradition; Flamenco is structured by cante, guitar, dance, and specific rhythmic palos.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Country
description: A broad American popular-music field developed from southern rural string-band, ballad, blues, gospel, cowboy, and commercial radio traditions, spanning acoustic roots styles through Nashville, honky-tonk, and contemporary production.
classificationHint: Use this broad label when country vocal phrasing, songwriting, and instrumentation are clear but no narrower style fits; prefer Honky Tonk, Bluegrass, or Western Swing when their defining traits dominate.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Folk
distinguishFrom.difference: Country is a commercial genre tradition with recognizable vocal and instrumental conventions; Folk is a broader community and singer-songwriter category.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Honky Tonk
distinguishFrom.difference: Honky Tonk is a specific hard-edged barroom branch of Country with dance rhythm and steel guitar.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Western Swing
distinguishFrom.difference: Western Swing is a jazz- and dance-band-influenced branch of Country rather than the general category.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Cretan
description: Traditional music of Crete centered on sung poetry and social dance, commonly led by Cretan lyra or violin with laouto, and including forms such as syrtos, pentozali, sousta, rizitika, and improvised mantinades.
classificationHint: Use when Cretan repertory, lyra-laouto texture, dance form, dialect, or provenance is clear; do not use for all Greek folk music or for bouzouki-led urban Rebetiko.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Rebetiko
distinguishFrom.difference: Cretan is a regional island tradition led by lyra/laouto and dance repertory; Rebetiko is an urban mainland/port-city song culture strongly linked to bouzouki.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Dangdut
description: Indonesian popular dance music that grew from Malay orchestra traditions and blends Indian film-music inflection, syncopated hand-drum patterns, flute, electric guitar, keyboards, and emotionally ornamented Indonesian or regional-language vocals.
classificationHint: Use when the characteristic dangdut drum groove, Malay-Indonesian vocal style, and popular-band arrangement are present; do not infer it from Indonesian language or tabla-like percussion alone.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Fado
description: Portuguese urban song joining music and poetry, typically performed by a solo singer with Portuguese guitarra and steel-string acoustic guitar, and known for flexible phrasing and themes of fate, longing, city life, and saudade.
classificationHint: Use when Portuguese guitarra, fado vocal delivery, repertory, and cultural setting are identifiable; melancholy acoustic song alone is not sufficient.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Flamenco
description: An Andalusian expressive tradition uniting cante singing, baile dance, and toque guitar across distinct palos, with characteristic modes, compás cycles, melisma, handclaps, and percussive footwork.
classificationHint: Use when flamenco cante, guitar vocabulary, compás, or a documented palo is central; Spanish language, acoustic guitar, or dramatic singing alone does not establish Flamenco.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Copla
distinguishFrom.difference: Flamenco follows specific cante, toque, and compás traditions; Copla is a theatrical orchestrated Spanish popular-song form.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Andalusian Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Flamenco is southern Spanish and palo-based; Andalusian Classical is a North African modal-suite art-music tradition.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Folk
description: A broad category for traditional community repertories and modern music modeled on them, emphasizing orally transmitted songs, ballads, dances, acoustic instruments, collective memory, or singer-songwriter interpretation.
classificationHint: Use only when traditional repertory, community function, or an explicit folk-revival aesthetic is present; acoustic instrumentation alone does not separate Folk from Country, Pop, or regional traditions.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Country
distinguishFrom.difference: Folk emphasizes traditional repertory, community transmission, or revival practice; Country is a specific American commercial genre field.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Funaná
description: A fast Cape Verdean music and dance tradition, especially associated with Santiago, driven by diatonic accordion and scraped ferrinho in tightly repeated rhythms; modern groups may add drums, bass, guitar, and keyboards.
classificationHint: Use when the rapid accordion-ferrinho Cape Verdean groove is central; accordion-led Forró or Zydeco belongs to different regional rhythmic and cultural traditions.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Gamelan
description: A family of Indonesian ensemble traditions, especially Javanese and Balinese, built from tuned gongs, metallophones, drums, and other instruments whose interlocking layers, cyclical time structure, and tuning are specific to each ensemble.
classificationHint: Use when a gamelan ensemble or clearly gamelan-derived compositional system is central; metallic percussion or interlocking patterns alone do not establish regional provenance or tradition.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Ghazal
description: A sung interpretation of the ghazal poetic form, whose autonomous rhymed couplets often explore love, separation, or spiritual longing; South Asian performance typically uses an intimate light-classical vocal style with harmonium, tabla, and melodic accompaniment.
classificationHint: Use when the ghazal text form and recital-like expressive singing are central; Qawwali is a participatory Sufi devotional ensemble practice with repeated refrains and rising intensity.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Qawwali
distinguishFrom.difference: Ghazal is a poetic art-song form usually presented intimately; Qawwali is a communal Sufi devotional performance with chorus, clapping, and cumulative intensity.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Gospel
description: Christian sacred music rooted especially in African American worship, joining spirituals and hymns with call-and-response, powerful lead singing, choir harmony, rhythmic accompaniment, and later blues, jazz, soul, or contemporary production.
classificationHint: Use when explicitly Christian devotional text and gospel vocal or church-performance language are central; soulful singing without sacred content belongs under Soul, while non-gospel liturgical music needs a different label.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Griot
description: A role- and lineage-based category for hereditary or professional West African oral historians, praise singers, genealogists, poets, and musicians whose repertories may use voice, kora, ngoni, balafon, or other region-specific instruments.
classificationHint: Use only when the performer, repertory, or social function is documented as griot/jeli/gewel tradition; narrative singing or a kora by itself does not establish the role, and Griot is not one musical genre.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Hawaiian
description: A broad family of Native Hawaiian and local island music encompassing mele chant, hula song, multipart hymnody, slack-key guitar, steel guitar, and later string-band forms shaped by Indigenous and introduced traditions.
classificationHint: Use when Hawaiian language, mele or hula function, slack-key/steel-guitar idiom, or documented Hawaiian context is clear; use Pacific only when a more specific island tradition cannot be identified.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Pacific
distinguishFrom.difference: Hawaiian identifies music of Hawai?i and its specific traditions; Pacific is a broad multi-island regional umbrella.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Highlife
description: A Ghanaian and Nigerian popular dance-music family that blends local rhythmic and melodic practices with brass-band, guitar-band, jazz, and Caribbean influences, often featuring interlocking guitars, horns, vocals, and a buoyant syncopated pulse.
classificationHint: Use when West African highlife guitar or dance-band language is clear; Afrobeat is generally more extended, funk-driven, and politically declamatory, while Soukous uses Congolese rumba-derived guitar structures.

distinguishFrom.label: Funk / Soul---Afrobeat
distinguishFrom.difference: Highlife favors compact Ghanaian/Nigerian dance-song and guitar/horn styles; Afrobeat uses longer funk-derived grooves and larger polyrhythmic arrangements.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Soukous
distinguishFrom.difference: Highlife is West African and rooted in Ghanaian/Nigerian dance bands; Soukous is Congolese and derived from Congolese rumba.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Hillbilly
description: A historical record-industry term for early commercial rural southern U.S. music, including string bands, old-time fiddle tunes, ballads, early country singing, and related sacred or comic material, especially from the 1920s?1940s.
classificationHint: Use chiefly for historically documented early recordings or revival performances explicitly adopting that period style; do not use it as a general synonym for modern Country or Appalachian music.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Country
distinguishFrom.difference: Hillbilly is a historical industry umbrella for early rural southern recordings; Country is the later and broader genre name.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Appalachian Music
distinguishFrom.difference: Hillbilly is a commercial historical category; Appalachian music is a regional tradition that extends beyond those recordings.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Hindustani
description: The classical music tradition of North India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, developing rāga through improvised ālāp and metered sections within tāla, in vocal genres or on instruments such as sitar, sarod, bansuri, sarangi, tabla, and tanpura.
classificationHint: Use for documented North Indian classical rāga performance and Hindustani concert grammar; Carnatic is the separate South Indian system, while Indian Classical is the umbrella when the branch is uncertain.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Carnatic
distinguishFrom.difference: Hindustani is the North Indian classical tradition with different repertory and concert structures; Carnatic is the South Indian system.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Indian Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Hindustani is one specific branch of the broader Indian Classical category.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Honky Tonk
description: A hard-edged country style associated with mid-century barrooms and dance halls, featuring direct themes of love, drinking, and loss, nasal or forceful vocals, steady dance rhythm, fiddle, piano, and prominent steel or electric guitar.
classificationHint: Use when the barroom subject matter, two-step pulse, and twanging steel/electric country arrangement dominate; broader polished Nashville or roots-country recordings should remain Country.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Country
distinguishFrom.difference: Honky Tonk is a specific barroom dance style within the broader Country field.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Western Swing
distinguishFrom.difference: Honky Tonk is song-centered and hard-edged; Western Swing emphasizes jazz harmony, ensemble swing, and instrumental solos.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Indian Classical
description: An umbrella for the major South Asian art-music systems centered on rāga, tāla, disciplined transmission, composition, and improvisation, principally the Hindustani tradition of the north and Carnatic tradition of the south.
classificationHint: Use only when Indian classical practice is clear but the northern or southern branch cannot be assigned; prefer Hindustani or Carnatic whenever repertory, ensemble, or concert structure identifies it.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Hindustani
distinguishFrom.difference: Hindustani is the northern branch; Indian Classical is the broader umbrella.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Carnatic
distinguishFrom.difference: Carnatic is the southern branch; Indian Classical is the broader umbrella.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Kaseko
description: An Afro-Surinamese popular dance style combining call-and-response vocals, layered percussion and the large skratji drum with brass, reeds, bass, guitar, and influences from kawina, marching bands, jazz, calypso, and Caribbean music.
classificationHint: Use when Surinamese context and the percussion-plus-brass Kaseko drive are identifiable; Soca and Highlife may share bright dance-band energy but belong to different regional traditions.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Klezmer
description: The instrumental dance-music tradition of Ashkenazi Jewish communities, shaped by modal ornament, expressive clarinet or violin phrasing, and repertories such as freylekhs, bulgars, horas, and doinas for celebrations and listening.
classificationHint: Use when Ashkenazi dance repertory and klezmer ornamentation are clear; minor-mode clarinet alone is insufficient, and Mizrahi denotes different Jewish traditions rooted in the Middle East and North Africa.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Mizrahi
distinguishFrom.difference: Klezmer is Ashkenazi Eastern European dance music; Mizrahi draws on Middle Eastern and North African Jewish musical languages.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Romani
distinguishFrom.difference: Klezmer is an Ashkenazi Jewish repertory tradition; Romani is a broad set of distinct Roma community traditions despite historical exchange.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Laïkó
description: Greek urban popular song that developed after Rebetiko, typically featuring bouzouki, amplified ensemble, direct melodic vocals, and themes of love and everyday life, later ranging from classic 1950s–70s styles to modern popular production.
classificationHint: Use for mainstream bouzouki-centered Greek popular song; Rebetiko is the earlier working-class urban tradition, while Éntekhno emphasizes literary composition and art-song arrangement.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Rebetiko
distinguishFrom.difference: Laïkó is the later mainstream Greek popular-song development; Rebetiko is the earlier urban working-class tradition.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Éntekhno
distinguishFrom.difference: Laïkó favors direct popular song and bouzouki style; Éntekhno emphasizes literary text and composed art-song treatment.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Luk Thung
description: Thai country popular music that emerged in the mid-twentieth century, featuring ornamented Thai vocals and songs about rural life, migration, work, romance, and social change over ensembles that may mix regional instruments with brass, guitars, strings, and electronics.
classificationHint: Use when Thai rural-pop identity and Luk Thung vocal phrasing are clear; Phleng Phuea Chiwit is more explicitly socially critical and folk-rock oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Phleng Phuea Chiwit
distinguishFrom.difference: Luk Thung centers rural popular song and highly ornamented vocals; Phleng Phuea Chiwit centers socially conscious “songs for life” and folk-rock language.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Maloya
description: A music, song, and dance tradition of Réunion created from Malagasy and African plantation histories, traditionally using solo-and-chorus singing with roulèr drum, kayamb rattle, pikèr, and cyclical percussion for ritual, remembrance, protest, and social performance.
classificationHint: Use when Réunion context, Maloya call-and-response, and its distinctive percussion cycle are central; Séga is a related Indian Ocean Creole dance family with a different rhythmic and social history.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Séga
distinguishFrom.difference: Maloya is Réunionnais, call-and-response, and rooted in ritual/percussion cycles; Séga is a broader Indian Ocean Creole dance tradition with its own frame-drum grooves.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Mbalax
description: Senegalese urban dance music, especially associated with Wolof performers, that places complex sabar drum language and rapid rhythmic breaks inside modern vocal, electric-guitar, bass, keyboard, and horn arrangements.
classificationHint: Use when sabar-derived Senegalese rhythmic phrasing is the defining engine; Highlife uses different West African guitar and horn traditions, and Soukous centers Congolese rumba-derived guitars.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Highlife
distinguishFrom.difference: Mbalax is Senegalese and driven by sabar rhythmic language; Highlife is Ghanaian/Nigerian guitar- and dance-band music.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Soukous
distinguishFrom.difference: Mbalax centers Senegalese sabar patterns; Soukous centers Congolese rumba-derived guitar interplay and sebene sections.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Min'yō
description: Japanese folk-song repertories tied to local work, festivals, dance, travel, or community identity, commonly sung in regionally distinctive styles with shamisen, shakuhachi, fue, taiko, hand percussion, or unaccompanied voice.
classificationHint: Use for documented Japanese regional folk song or a faithful revival arrangement; Japanese scales, shamisen, or festival drums alone do not distinguish Min’yō from theater, art music, or modern composition.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Mizrahi
description: A broad Israeli popular-music field drawing on Jewish musical traditions from the Middle East and North Africa, commonly combining Hebrew vocals, Arab and Mediterranean modes, ornamented singing, regional instruments, and modern pop production.
classificationHint: Use when documented Mizrahi identity and Middle Eastern/North African Jewish musical language are central; do not apply to all Israeli music or to Ashkenazi Klezmer.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Klezmer
distinguishFrom.difference: Mizrahi draws on Middle Eastern and North African Jewish traditions; Klezmer is Ashkenazi Eastern European instrumental dance music.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Nhạc Vàng
description: A Vietnamese sentimental popular-song field associated especially with pre-1975 southern Vietnam and its diaspora, known for direct themes of love, separation, war, and exile, often set to slow bolero, rumba, tango, or restrained orchestral/electric arrangements.
classificationHint: Use when documented Nhạc Vàng repertory, South Vietnamese historical context, or its characteristic sentimental vocal and bolero-based style is present; Vietnamese balladry in general is not automatically Nhạc Vàng.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Nordic
description: A broad umbrella for traditional and revival music of Scandinavia and the North Atlantic, including fiddle dance repertories, ballads, herding calls, runo or joik-related traditions, and region-specific instruments and vocal practices.
classificationHint: Use when a Nordic regional repertory or documented cultural context is present; it is not shorthand for cold, atmospheric, folk-influenced production.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Celtic
distinguishFrom.difference: Nordic refers to Scandinavian and North Atlantic traditions; Celtic refers to Atlantic Celtic-language regions and their diasporas.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Népzene
description: Hungarian traditional folk music, encompassing regional vocal styles, old- and new-style songs, verbunk and csárdás dance repertory, and ensembles using voice, fiddle, viola, double bass, cimbalom, winds, or zithers.
classificationHint: Use for documented Hungarian folk repertory or regionally characteristic performance; Romani musicians have deeply shaped performance practice, but Romani music is a wider transnational category.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Romani
distinguishFrom.difference: Népzene identifies Hungarian folk repertory; Romani identifies diverse Roma community traditions extending across many countries.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Ottoman Classical
description: The courtly and urban art music of the Ottoman sphere, organized through makam modal development and usul rhythmic cycles in vocal and instrumental forms such as peşrev, saz semaisi, şarkı, and fasıl suites.
classificationHint: Use for composed Ottoman/Turkish classical repertory and makam-usul performance practice; do not equate any oud or ney recording with Ottoman Classical.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Persian Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Ottoman Classical uses the makam and usul systems; Persian Classical organizes improvisation and composition through dastgāh and radif.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Andalusian Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Ottoman Classical belongs to the Ottoman makam tradition; Andalusian Classical refers to North African nūba lineages.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Overtone Singing
description: A family of vocal techniques in which a singer shapes resonances above a sustained fundamental so that one or more overtones become separately audible, prominent in several traditions including Tuvan khöömei and Mongolian khöömii.
classificationHint: Use when overtone isolation is a primary, audible performance technique; throat timbre, drones, or cultural association alone are insufficient, and the label does not specify one regional repertory.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Pacific
description: A broad geographic umbrella for the many distinct Indigenous and local music traditions of Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia, including community song, dance, chant, percussion, string-band, choral, ceremonial, and contemporary forms.
classificationHint: Use only when Pacific Island provenance is clear but no specific culture or island tradition is available; do not infer it from ukulele, ocean imagery, choral texture, or generalized “island” production.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Hawaiian
distinguishFrom.difference: Pacific is a broad multi-island umbrella; Hawaiian identifies the specific traditions of Hawaiʻi.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Pasodoble
description: A brisk Spanish duple-meter march and partner dance associated with military bands, bullring spectacle, fiestas, and ballroom repertory, usually marked by emphatic accents and bright brass or orchestral writing.
classificationHint: Use when the characteristic march-like duple rhythm and Spanish pasodoble arrangement define the track; Flamenco follows different palos and compás cycles.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Flamenco
distinguishFrom.difference: Pasodoble is a march-derived duple dance; Flamenco is a family of cante, guitar, and dance palos with distinct compás patterns.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Persian Classical
description: The classical art music of Iran, organized through the radif repertory and dastgāh modal system, balancing memorized melodic models with improvisation in vocal or instrumental performance on tār, setār, santur, kamancheh, ney, tombak, and related instruments.
classificationHint: Use for documented Persian classical radif-dastgāh practice; Ottoman Classical follows makam and usul structures, while generic Iranian folk or pop should not receive this label.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Ottoman Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Persian Classical is organized through radif and dastgāh; Ottoman Classical uses makam, usul, and Ottoman suite/forms.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Phleng Phuea Chiwit
description: Thai “songs for life,” a socially conscious popular-music movement shaped by protest song, Thai folk sources, and rock instrumentation, with lyrics about workers, rural communities, inequality, politics, and national life.
classificationHint: Use when Thai socially engaged songwriting and the movement’s folk-rock aesthetic are central; Luk Thung may address rural experience but is a broader country-pop tradition.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Luk Thung
distinguishFrom.difference: Phleng Phuea Chiwit foregrounds social critique and folk-rock songwriting; Luk Thung is the broader Thai rural country-pop tradition.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Polka
description: A lively Central European couple dance in duple meter, commonly using an oom-pah accompaniment and performed by folk, brass, accordion, string, or dance orchestras across many regional traditions.
classificationHint: Use when the specific polka dance rhythm and phrasing are clear; accordion or brass-band instrumentation alone is insufficient, and Volksmusik is a broader German-speaking folk category.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Volksmusik
distinguishFrom.difference: Polka is a specific duple dance form; Volksmusik is a broad cultural and repertory category that may include polkas among many other forms.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Qawwali
description: A Sufi devotional performance tradition of South Asia led by one or more singers with responding chorus, handclaps, harmonium, and dholak or tabla, building repeated poetic and melodic phrases toward collective spiritual intensity.
classificationHint: Use when the qawwal party format, Sufi devotional text, responsorial repetition, and intensifying performance arc are clear; Ghazal is a poetic art-song form and need not be devotional or communal.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Ghazal
distinguishFrom.difference: Qawwali is a communal Sufi devotional ensemble practice; Ghazal is a poetic art-song form usually presented with a more intimate recital structure.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Raï
description: Algerian popular song that developed from western Algerian urban and rural traditions, known for candid social and romantic lyrics, ornamented Arabic vocals, and a blend of gasba flute, percussion, trumpet, accordion, synthesizers, drum machines, and modern pop production.
classificationHint: Use when Algerian Raï vocal phrasing, repertory, or documented context is clear; Arabic-language pop or North African instrumentation alone is insufficient.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Rebetiko
description: A Greek urban song and dance tradition that spread among lower- and working-class communities in the early twentieth century, associated with bouzouki or earlier small ensembles, modal melody, zeibekiko and hasapiko rhythms, and lyrics about marginal or everyday life.
classificationHint: Use for the historically and stylistically grounded Rebetiko repertory; Laïkó is its later mainstream popular-song development, while Cretan music is a separate regional folk tradition.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Laïkó
distinguishFrom.difference: Rebetiko is the earlier urban working-class tradition; Laïkó is its later, more mainstream popular-song development.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Cretan
distinguishFrom.difference: Rebetiko is urban and bouzouki-associated; Cretan music centers island dance repertory and lyra/laouto performance.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Romani
description: A broad, non-unified label for music made within diverse Roma communities across Europe and beyond, encompassing distinct local vocal, dance, instrumental, and professional traditions shaped by each region.
classificationHint: Use only with documented Roma cultural, performer, or repertory context; rapid violin, ornamented singing, or a stereotyped “Gypsy” sound is not sufficient evidence.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Klezmer
distinguishFrom.difference: Romani is a broad set of Roma traditions; Klezmer is a specific Ashkenazi Jewish dance repertory despite historical musical exchange.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Népzene
distinguishFrom.difference: Romani denotes Roma community traditions; Népzene denotes Hungarian folk repertory, often performed by both Roma and non-Roma musicians.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Salegy
description: A fast Malagasy dance-music style associated especially with northern Madagascar, built on driving compound-meter rhythms, syncopated guitar or accordion patterns, electric bass, percussion, call-and-response vocals, and energetic breakdowns.
classificationHint: Use when the northern Malagasy Salegy rhythm and performance arc are identifiable; Soukous may share bright electric guitars but follows Congolese rumba-derived phrasing.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Soukous
distinguishFrom.difference: Salegy uses a Malagasy compound-meter dance rhythm; Soukous follows Congolese rumba-derived guitar and sebene structures.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Sea Shanties
description: Maritime work songs whose repeated call-and-response phrases coordinated group labor such as hauling lines, raising anchor, or working a capstan; the required rhythm and form vary with the shipboard task.
classificationHint: Use for functional or revival performances of maritime work-song forms; sea-themed ballads without a labor-coordinating refrain are maritime Folk, not automatically shanties.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Folk
distinguishFrom.difference: Sea Shanties have task-shaped maritime call-and-response forms; Folk is the broader category containing many non-work songs.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Soukous
description: A fast Congolese dance-music development from Congolese rumba, characterized by layered high-register electric guitars, buoyant bass and percussion, sung opening sections, and extended sebene passages that intensify the groove.
classificationHint: Use when Congolese rumba-derived guitar interplay and an extended dance-focused sebene are central; Highlife is West African, while Salegy uses a distinct Malagasy compound-meter rhythm.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Highlife
distinguishFrom.difference: Soukous is Congolese and rumba-derived; Highlife is rooted in Ghanaian and Nigerian guitar and dance-band traditions.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Salegy
distinguishFrom.difference: Soukous uses Congolese rumba and sebene guitar structures; Salegy is Malagasy and driven by a different compound-meter pulse.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Séga
description: An Indian Ocean Creole music and dance family associated especially with Mauritius, Réunion, Rodrigues, and Seychelles, traditionally using improvised Creole vocals, frame drum such as ravanne, rattles, triangle, and a swaying rhythm that may gradually accelerate.
classificationHint: Use when documented Indian Ocean Creole Séga context and frame-drum dance rhythm are present; Maloya is a distinct Réunion tradition with stronger ritual call-and-response roots.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Maloya
distinguishFrom.difference: Séga is an Indian Ocean Creole dance family centered on its frame-drum groove; Maloya is a Réunionnais ritual and protest tradition with different percussion cycles.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Volksmusik
description: A broad German-language term for traditional and tradition-oriented music of German-speaking Central Europe and Alpine regions, including regional songs, dances, brass ensembles, accordions, zithers, and community repertory.
classificationHint: Use when German/Austrian/Swiss regional folk context or repertory is clear; do not use it merely for accordion music, and use Polka when that specific dance form is identifiable.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Polka
distinguishFrom.difference: Volksmusik is a broad regional category; Polka is one specific duple-meter dance that may occur within it.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Western Swing
description: A southwestern U.S. dance-band style that combines country fiddle and steel guitar with jazz swing rhythm, horn or reed arrangements, blues, pop standards, and extensive instrumental improvisation.
classificationHint: Use when a country ensemble plays with clear swing feel, jazz harmony, and rotating solos; Honky Tonk is more song-centered and rhythmically straight, while Big Band lacks the country string and steel-guitar core.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Country
distinguishFrom.difference: Western Swing is a jazz-influenced dance-band branch of the broader Country field.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Honky Tonk
distinguishFrom.difference: Western Swing emphasizes ensemble swing and instrumental solos; Honky Tonk emphasizes direct barroom songs and a straighter dance pulse.

distinguishFrom.label: Jazz---Big Band
distinguishFrom.difference: Western Swing retains country fiddle, steel guitar, and repertory; Big Band is organized around a jazz horn section.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Zouk
description: A polished French Antillean dance-pop style developed in the 1980s, especially in Guadeloupe and Martinique, combining Caribbean rhythms with prominent bass, synthesizers, drum machines, horns or guitars, and French or Antillean Creole vocals.
classificationHint: Use when French Antillean Zouk repertory, vocal context, and sleek syncopated dance production are clear; Compas is Haitian guitar-band music, and generic tropical synth-pop is not enough.

distinguishFrom.label: Latin---Compas
distinguishFrom.difference: Zouk is French Antillean synth-oriented dance-pop; Compas is a Haitian guitar-band tradition with a steadier continuous groove.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Zydeco
description: Black Creole dance music from southwest Louisiana, commonly using accordion and frottoir rubboard with drums, bass, guitar, and vocals, and drawing strongly on blues, rhythm-and-blues, and Creole French traditions.
classificationHint: Use when rubboard-driven rhythm, Black Creole context, and blues/R&B-inflected accordion dance music are evident; Cajun uses a related accordion-fiddle vocabulary but a different community lineage and repertory.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Cajun
distinguishFrom.difference: Zydeco is a Black Creole, rubboard-driven style with blues/R&B influence; Cajun centers Acadian French fiddle-and-accordion repertory.

label: Folk, World, & Country---Éntekhno
description: A Greek art-pop and composed-song tradition that emerged around the 1960s, setting literary or poetic texts in carefully arranged music that bridges Greek folk elements, orchestral writing, and modern singer-songwriter practice.
classificationHint: Use when literary Greek song and deliberate composed arrangement are central; Laïkó is more directly popular and bouzouki-led, while Rebetiko belongs to an earlier urban folk lineage.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Laïkó
distinguishFrom.difference: Éntekhno emphasizes literary text and art-song composition; Laïkó favors direct mainstream Greek popular style.

distinguishFrom.label: Folk, World, & Country---Rebetiko
distinguishFrom.difference: Éntekhno is a postwar composed art-song field; Rebetiko is an earlier orally transmitted urban song tradition.

label: Funk / Soul---Afrobeat
description: Groove-based music combining West African rhythm, funk, horns, and extended band arrangements.
classificationHint: Use this when interlocking percussion, horns, and long funk grooves suggest Afrobeat.

label: Funk / Soul---Bayou Funk
description: Louisiana-rooted funk that blends deep syncopated rhythm, earthy soul and R&B, horn or organ accents, and the loose, humid feel of New Orleans and Gulf Coast music.
classificationHint: Use this when a raw funk groove carries clear Louisiana character through second-line-influenced rhythm, regional vocal style, or swampy horn-and-organ arrangement.

label: Funk / Soul---Boogie
description: Late-1970s and 1980s post-disco dance music combining funk basslines and soulful vocals with synthesizers, drum machines, polished rhythm guitar, and a steady mid-tempo groove.
classificationHint: Use this when funk and disco songwriting is recast with prominent electronic bass, synths, and drum-machine production without becoming house music.

label: Funk / Soul---Contemporary R&B
description: Modern R&B with smooth vocals, polished production, and soul-influenced harmony.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has current R&B vocal style and production rather than older soul or funk.

label: Funk / Soul---Disco
description: Funk and soul-rooted dance music with steady beat, bass groove, strings or horns, and classic disco feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track sounds disco from a live-band funk/soul perspective.

label: Funk / Soul---Free Funk
description: An experimental fusion of funk's repeating rhythmic foundation with free-jazz improvisation, open form, dissonance, and unpredictable ensemble interaction.
classificationHint: Use this when a persistent funk pulse supports genuinely free or avant-garde improvisation rather than ordinary solos inside a fixed funk arrangement.

label: Funk / Soul---Funk
description: Groove-centered music with syncopated bass, tight drums, rhythmic guitar, and strong physical feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the rhythm section and groove are the main identity.

label: Funk / Soul---Gogo
description: Washington, D.C. funk built around continuous live grooves, congas and auxiliary percussion, call-and-response vocals, and direct interaction with a dancing audience.
classificationHint: Use this when layered hand percussion and a band-led, unbroken call-and-response groove are central; the live communal flow matters more than a conventional verse-chorus form.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Go-Go
distinguishFrom.difference: The sound is the same Washington, D.C. tradition; use Funk / Soul when continuous live-band groove leads, and Hip Hop when rap or MC performance is the primary frame.

label: Funk / Soul---Gospel
description: Soul or funk-related gospel music with religious lyrics, church-derived vocals, and strong group or lead singing.
classificationHint: Use this when gospel vocal style and religious context are central.

label: Funk / Soul---Minneapolis Sound
description: A Prince-associated fusion of funk, rock, soul, new wave, and synth-pop, marked by electronic drums, bright synthesizers, sharp guitars, and a lean, highly arranged groove.
classificationHint: Use this when 1980s-style funk and R&B combine with prominent drum-machine programming, synth hooks, and rock guitar in the distinctive Minneapolis lineage.

label: Funk / Soul---Neo Soul
description: Modern soul style with warm vocals, jazz/R&B harmony, and organic or understated production.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels contemporary but rooted in classic soul and R&B.

label: Funk / Soul---New Jack Swing
description: Late-1980s/1990s R&B style combining swingbeat rhythms, hip-hop drums, and polished vocal hooks.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has the distinctive swung R&B/hip-hop groove of New Jack Swing.

label: Funk / Soul---P.Funk
description: The Parliament-Funkadelic lineage of expansive psychedelic funk, featuring elastic bass, layered ensemble grooves, synthesizers, rock guitar, group vocals, and theatrical science-fiction imagery.
classificationHint: Use this when a heavy communal funk groove is paired with psychedelic production, prominent synth or guitar layers, and the playful cosmic aesthetic associated with P-Funk.

label: Funk / Soul---Psychedelic
description: Psychedelic soul and funk that expands gospel- and R&B-rooted songwriting with distorted guitars, studio effects, extended arrangements, unusual textures, and countercultural atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when soul or funk remains the rhythmic and vocal foundation but psychedelic effects, rock instrumentation, or exploratory structure substantially reshape the sound.

label: Funk / Soul---Rhythm & Blues
description: Postwar African-American popular music combining blues and boogie patterns, gospel-inflected vocals, jazz or horn-band instrumentation, and a strong danceable backbeat.
classificationHint: Use this for classic rhythm and blues whose shuffle, backbeat, blues form, and vocal-or-horn arrangement predate contemporary R&B production.

label: Funk / Soul---Soul
description: Vocal-centered music rooted in gospel, rhythm and blues, and expressive emotional performance.
classificationHint: Use this when soulful singing and groove are central but no narrower soul subtype dominates.

label: Funk / Soul---Swingbeat
description: Late-1980s and early-1990s R&B that fuses soulful singing with hip-hop-derived drum-machine production and a conspicuously swung, bouncing rhythmic grid.
classificationHint: Use this when polished R&B vocals sit over hard programmed drums with an audible shuffle or swing; it substantially overlaps with New Jack Swing.

distinguishFrom.label: Funk / Soul---New Jack Swing
distinguishFrom.difference: Swingbeat is commonly used as an alternate or closely overlapping name; New Jack Swing more specifically denotes the Teddy Riley-associated R&B and hip-hop fusion movement.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---RnB/Swing
distinguishFrom.difference: RnB/Swing is the hip-hop-facing crossover label; Swingbeat foregrounds the swung rhythmic production within R&B.

label: Funk / Soul---UK Street Soul
description: Independent British soul and R&B from the late 1980s and early 1990s, combining intimate vocals with DIY drum-machine grooves, synthesizers, deep bass, and UK sound-system influence.
classificationHint: Use this when understated British R&B or soul has a raw home-studio character, weighty programmed rhythm, and underground rather than glossy US production.

label: Hip Hop---Bass Music
description: Bass-focused hip-hop and rap production in which powerful sub-bass, heavy drum-machine impact, and low-frequency pressure dominate the track.
classificationHint: Use this broad label when a hip-hop track is defined more by extreme low end and bass-system impact than by a clearer regional or stylistic subtype.

label: Hip Hop---Beatbox
description: Music built around vocal percussion, using the mouth and voice to imitate drums, bass, scratches, and other rhythmic sounds.
classificationHint: Use this when human vocal percussion is the primary rhythmic performance rather than a brief effect layered over a conventional beat.

label: Hip Hop---Boom Bap
description: Classic hip-hop style with hard drums, sample loops, and a head-nod rhythm.
classificationHint: Use this when the beat has crisp kicks/snares and sample-based 1990s-style hip-hop feel.

label: Hip Hop---Bounce
description: A fast, participatory New Orleans hip-hop style built from repetitive sampled beats, call-and-response chants, dance commands, and energetic party delivery.
classificationHint: Use this when New Orleans-style chant hooks, rapid dance call-outs, and a looping Triggerman-type beat define the track.

label: Hip Hop---Britcore
description: British hardcore hip-hop associated with the late 1980s and early 1990s, combining forceful UK rap with dense sampling, hard breakbeats, and urgent production.
