description: Accessible, pleasant orchestral or popular instrumental music designed for easy listening and light entertainment.
classificationHint: Use this when the music is polished, gentle, and entertainment-oriented without strong genre-specific identity.

distinguishFrom.label: Jazz---Easy Listening
distinguishFrom.difference: Easy Listening may overlap but often comes from jazz/pop arrangements; Light Music can be more orchestral or broadcast-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Score
distinguishFrom.difference: Score is media-specific; Light Music is a general listening category.

label: Pop---Music Hall
description: Popular entertainment song style associated with stage variety, theatrical delivery, and older British performance traditions.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has theatrical, vaudeville-like, or old stage-entertainment character.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Musical
distinguishFrom.difference: Musical implies narrative theatre songs; Music Hall is older variety-entertainment song style.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Novelty
distinguishFrom.difference: Novelty is broader and joke-oriented; Music Hall is a specific stage tradition.

label: Pop---Novelty
description: Pop or entertainment music built around humor, gimmicks, unusual concepts, or intentionally silly hooks.
classificationHint: Use this when the main identity is comic, strange, gimmicky, or novelty-driven rather than normal pop songwriting.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Parody
distinguishFrom.difference: Parody specifically imitates or mocks another work or style; Novelty is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Break-In
distinguishFrom.difference: Break-In is a specific novelty format using inserted clips.

label: Pop---Parody
description: Music that imitates or reworks another song, artist, or style for comic or satirical effect.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly a humorous imitation or rewrite rather than simply a novelty song.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Novelty
distinguishFrom.difference: Novelty is broader; Parody specifically targets another work, artist, or style.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Parody
distinguishFrom.difference: Rock Parody is more guitar/band-based; Pop Parody may use broader pop formats.

label: Pop---Schlager
description: Germanic popular music with simple melodies, sentimental or cheerful lyrics, and singalong entertainment appeal.
classificationHint: Use this for German/Austrian/European-style easy singalong pop with sentimental or party-oriented mainstream character.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Europop
distinguishFrom.difference: Europop is broader and more modern-pop oriented; Schlager is more singalong and sentimental/entertainment focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Disco Polo
distinguishFrom.difference: Disco Polo is specifically Polish dance-pop; Schlager is broader Germanic popular entertainment.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Levenslied
distinguishFrom.difference: Levenslied is specifically Dutch and usually more everyday-sentimental.

label: Pop---Vocal
description: Pop or popular music where the lead vocal performance is the main focus.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is best categorized by prominent vocals and pop-song structure, without a more specific pop subgenre being clear.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Ballad
distinguishFrom.difference: Ballad is slower and more emotional; Vocal is broader.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Chanson
distinguishFrom.difference: Chanson is specifically French lyric-driven song.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop is more beat and dancefloor-production oriented.

label: Reggae---Calypso
description: A Trinidad and Tobago song tradition built around syncopated Afro-Caribbean rhythm, memorable refrains, and narrative lyrics that often use wit, satire, or topical social commentary.
classificationHint: Use this when lyrical storytelling and calypso rhythm are central; do not treat it as Jamaican reggae merely because both belong to the Caribbean.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Soca
distinguishFrom.difference: Calypso prioritizes narrative songcraft and topical lyrics; Soca intensifies the rhythm and repeated hooks for carnival dancing.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Mento
distinguishFrom.difference: Calypso developed in Trinidad and Tobago; Mento is a distinct Jamaican acoustic folk tradition despite superficial Caribbean similarities.

label: Reggae---Dancehall
description: Jamaican popular style with digital rhythms, deejay vocals, and dance-oriented energy.
classificationHint: Use this when the rhythm and vocal delivery clearly fit dancehall rather than roots reggae.

label: Reggae---Dub
description: Reggae-derived style focused on bass, drums, echo, reverb, and stripped instrumental mixes.
classificationHint: Use this when dub mixing effects and bass-space are central.

label: Reggae---Dub Poetry
description: Rhythmically chanted poetry rooted in Jamaican and Black British culture, commonly addressing politics and social justice with cadences shaped by reggae and dub, with or without backing music.
classificationHint: Use this when spoken poetic performance—not singing or dancehall deejaying—is primary and its meter, language, or accompaniment is explicitly reggae-derived.

label: Reggae---Lovers Rock
description: A smooth, romantic reggae style developed strongly in Britain, pairing warm bass and restrained offbeat rhythm with soulful singing, close harmonies, and love-centered lyrics.
classificationHint: Use this when romantic vocals and polished soul influence dominate a gentle reggae arrangement rather than the political or Rastafari themes associated with roots reggae.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Roots Reggae
distinguishFrom.difference: Lovers Rock foregrounds romance, smooth soul vocals, and polished warmth; Roots Reggae foregrounds Rastafari, African consciousness, and social resistance.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Rocksteady
distinguishFrom.difference: Rocksteady is the earlier Jamaican transition from ska to reggae; Lovers Rock is a later, strongly British romantic reggae tradition influenced by its smooth vocal style.

label: Reggae---Mento
description: A Jamaican folk tradition predating ska and reggae, typically using acoustic guitar or banjo, hand percussion, and rumba box beneath humorous, topical, or everyday-life lyrics.
classificationHint: Use this for acoustic Jamaican folk rhythm and storytelling; distinguish it from Trinidadian Calypso and from the amplified bass-and-drum framework of reggae.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Calypso
distinguishFrom.difference: Mento is Jamaican acoustic folk music; Calypso is a Trinidad and Tobago song tradition with its own rhythmic and carnival history.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Rocksteady
distinguishFrom.difference: Mento is acoustic folk music that predates reggae; Rocksteady uses an amplified rhythm section, melodic electric bass, and soul-influenced vocals.

label: Reggae---Ragga
description: Digitally produced dancehall reggae that emerged in the 1980s, using drum machines, synthesized riddims, deep bass, and rhythmic deejay toasting rather than a conventional live band.
classificationHint: Use this when electronic dancehall production and patois deejay delivery are central; use Dancehall for the broader style regardless of analog or digital production.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Dancehall
distinguishFrom.difference: Dancehall is the broader Jamaican style and performance culture; Ragga specifically emphasizes its digital riddims and synthesized production.

label: Reggae---Reggae
description: Broad reggae style with offbeat rhythm, strong bass, relaxed groove, and Jamaican roots.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly reggae but no narrower reggae subtype dominates.

label: Reggae---Reggae Gospel
description: Christian gospel songwriting and worship themes performed through reggae rhythm, bass, offbeat accompaniment, and sometimes dancehall or roots-reggae production.
classificationHint: Use this only when both the religious gospel content and a clear reggae framework are essential; ordinary reggae with spiritual imagery is not automatically Gospel.

label: Reggae---Reggae-Pop
description: Accessible pop songwriting that incorporates reggae's offbeat guitar or keyboard pulse, bass-led groove, and Caribbean vocal inflection into concise, polished verse-chorus form.
classificationHint: Use this when pop hooks and commercial song structure lead while reggae rhythm remains clearly audible; use Pop Reggae only as the model's equivalent naming, not for generic tropical pop.

label: Reggae---Rocksteady
description: A mid-1960s Jamaican style that slowed ska into a spacious, bass-forward groove, reduced horn emphasis, and brought soulful lead vocals and harmony groups to the foreground.
classificationHint: Use this when the rhythm is slower and smoother than ska, with prominent melodic bass and soul-influenced singing, but predates the heavier one-drop language of mature reggae.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Roots Reggae
distinguishFrom.difference: Rocksteady is a mid-1960s transitional style with smooth soul vocals and melodic bass; Roots Reggae is later, rhythmically heavier, and defined strongly by cultural and spiritual themes.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Ska
distinguishFrom.difference: Ska is faster with a buoyant offbeat and stronger horn presence; Rocksteady slows the groove and foregrounds bass and vocals.

label: Reggae---Roots Reggae
description: Reggae centered on Rastafari consciousness, African identity, spiritual reflection, and resistance to oppression, carried by deep bass and one-drop, rockers, or steppers rhythms.
classificationHint: Use this when cultural, spiritual, or political roots themes are fundamental; the label describes both message and classic 1970s reggae practice, not simply an old recording.

label: Reggae---Ska
description: Upbeat Jamaican style with fast offbeat rhythm, horns, and dance energy.
classificationHint: Use this when ska rhythm is clearly present rather than slower reggae groove.

label: Reggae---Soca
description: High-energy carnival music from Trinidad and Tobago that modernized calypso with a denser dance pulse, prominent bass and percussion, repeated hooks, and strong crowd-participation drive.
classificationHint: Use this when fast carnival dance energy and repetitive participatory hooks outweigh calypso's narrative focus; it is Trinidadian rather than a reggae subtype.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Calypso
distinguishFrom.difference: Soca is denser, faster, and designed around continuous carnival dance energy; Calypso gives more space to lyrical narrative and topical commentary.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Steel Band
distinguishFrom.difference: Soca is a song and dance genre that may use steelpan; Steel Band identifies the performing ensemble and can arrange music from many genres.

label: Reggae---Steel Band
description: Ensemble music performed on tuned steelpans of different ranges, developed in Trinidad and Tobago and used for arranged calypso, soca, popular, and orchestral repertoire.
classificationHint: Use this when the bell-like pitched sound and layered orchestration of a steelpan ensemble define the recording, regardless of the particular composition being arranged.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Soca
distinguishFrom.difference: Steel Band describes instrumentation and ensemble format; Soca describes a carnival dance genre that can be played with or without steelpan.

distinguishFrom.label: Reggae---Calypso
distinguishFrom.difference: Steel Band describes the tuned-percussion ensemble; Calypso describes a lyrical Trinidadian song tradition often arranged for that ensemble.

label: Rock---AOR
description: Album-oriented rock with polished production, melodic hooks, and radio-friendly rock arrangements.
classificationHint: Use this for smooth, professional rock that sits between classic rock, soft rock, and arena-ready melodic rock.

label: Rock---Acid Rock
description: Psychedelic rock with heavier, rawer, and more distorted guitar sounds.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a late-1960s psychedelic feel but sounds heavier and more acid-drenched than general psychedelic rock.

label: Rock---Acoustic
description: Rock-oriented music arranged mainly with acoustic guitars or unplugged instrumentation.
classificationHint: Use this when the performance is rock/song based but the sound is primarily acoustic rather than electric.

label: Rock---Alternative Rock
description: Broad rock style outside mainstream classic-rock conventions, often with indie, post-punk, grunge, or experimental influence.
classificationHint: Use this as a broad label for rock tracks that sound alternative but not specific enough for grunge, indie rock, post-punk, or shoegaze.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Indie Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: Indie Rock usually has a more independent guitar-band feel; Alternative Rock is broader and may be heavier or more mainstream.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Grunge
distinguishFrom.difference: Grunge is darker, heavier, and more 1990s Seattle-associated.

label: Rock---Arena Rock
description: Large-scale rock built for big choruses, powerful drums, and stadium-sized performance.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has broad anthemic hooks and a big, polished rock sound.

label: Rock---Art Rock
description: Rock music with experimental, conceptual, or art-school influence, often using unusual structures or instrumentation.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly rock but more ambitious or unconventional than standard rock songwriting.

label: Rock---Atmospheric Black Metal
description: Black metal emphasizing mood, texture, and expansive atmosphere alongside harsh vocals and tremolo-driven guitars.
classificationHint: Use this when black metal elements are present but the main effect is immersive atmosphere rather than pure aggression.

label: Rock---Avantgarde
description: Rock that deliberately pushes structure, sound, or performance beyond conventional rock forms.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is rock-based but experimental enough that normal subgenres do not describe it well.

label: Rock---Beat
description: 1960s-style beat music with catchy guitar rhythms, vocal harmonies, and early pop-rock energy.
classificationHint: Use this for early British-invasion-like rock and pop-rock built around simple rhythmic guitar songs.

label: Rock---Black Metal
description: Extreme metal with harsh vocals, tremolo guitars, blast beats, and cold or occult atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has recognizable black metal sound rather than general extreme metal.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Death Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Death Metal is usually thicker and more riff/growl focused; Black Metal is colder, tremolo-heavy, and more atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Atmospheric Black Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Atmospheric Black Metal places more weight on immersion and texture.

label: Rock---Blues Rock
description: Rock music built from blues riffs, blues phrasing, guitar solos, and a strong blues-derived groove.
classificationHint: Use this when blues language is central but the arrangement and energy are clearly rock.

label: Rock---Brit Pop
description: British alternative pop-rock style with melodic songwriting, guitar-band sound, and 1990s UK character.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a British guitar-pop identity rather than generic indie or alternative rock.

label: Rock---Classic Rock
description: Broad rock style associated with older mainstream rock, guitar riffs, strong vocals, and conventional rock-band arrangement.
classificationHint: Use this when the track fits traditional rock vocabulary but no narrower label is clearly better.

label: Rock---Coldwave
description: Cold, minimal post-punk or synth-influenced rock with stark atmosphere and detached vocals.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels icy, minimal, and post-punk/new-wave related.

label: Rock---Country Rock
description: Rock music blended with country instrumentation, harmony, rhythm, or songwriting.
classificationHint: Use this when guitars and rock arrangement are present but country flavor is central.

label: Rock---Crust
description: Aggressive punk/metal crossover with raw production, political intensity, and harsh vocals.
classificationHint: Use this when the track combines punk speed and metal heaviness in a rough crust style.

label: Rock---Death Metal
description: Extreme metal with growled vocals, heavy distorted riffs, blast beats, and dark aggressive themes.
classificationHint: Use this when the sound is clearly death metal rather than thrash, black metal, or metalcore.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Black Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Black Metal is colder and more tremolo/atmosphere focused; Death Metal is heavier, growlier, and more riff-driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Technical Death Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Technical Death Metal is more complex and precise.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Thrash
distinguishFrom.difference: Thrash is faster and more riff-picking oriented but usually less growled and brutal.

label: Rock---Deathcore
description: Metalcore and death metal hybrid with breakdowns, growled vocals, and extreme-metal riffing.
classificationHint: Use this when death metal aggression is combined with modern hardcore/metalcore breakdown structure.

label: Rock---Deathrock
description: Dark punk-related rock with gothic atmosphere, theatrical vocals, and horror or death imagery.
classificationHint: Use this when the track sounds like gothic punk rather than goth rock or death metal.

label: Rock---Depressive Black Metal
description: Black metal focused on bleak, despairing atmosphere, slower passages, and anguished vocals.
classificationHint: Use this when black metal elements are present but the dominant mood is depressive and desolate.

label: Rock---Doo Wop
description: Vocal harmony pop-rock and rhythm-and-blues style with nonsense syllables, close harmonies, and 1950s feel.
classificationHint: Use this when vocal-group harmony is the defining feature.

label: Rock---Doom Metal
description: Slow, heavy metal with massive riffs, dark atmosphere, and a weighty, ominous feel.
classificationHint: Use this when heaviness comes from slow tempo and thick riffs rather than speed or technical aggression.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Sludge Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Sludge Metal is dirtier and more hardcore/noise influenced; Doom Metal is more traditional and slow-heavy.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Funeral Doom Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Funeral Doom is much slower, longer, and more mournful.

label: Rock---Dream Pop
description: Atmospheric pop-rock with soft vocals, reverb, and hazy melodic textures.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is song-based but dreamy, soft, and atmospheric.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Shoegaze
distinguishFrom.difference: Shoegaze is denser and more guitar-wall focused; Dream Pop is usually softer and more songlike.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Chillwave
distinguishFrom.difference: Chillwave is more electronic and lo-fi synth-pop oriented.

label: Rock---Emo
description: Emotionally expressive rock or punk-derived music with confessional vocals and melodic intensity.
classificationHint: Use this when the track centers on emotional vocal delivery and emo rock/punk aesthetics.

label: Rock---Ethereal
description: Very atmospheric, airy rock or gothic-related music with floating vocals and spacious textures.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels weightless, reverb-heavy, and more atmospheric than rhythm-driven.

label: Rock---Experimental
description: Rock that uses unusual structures, sounds, or performance methods while remaining rock-based.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly rock but does not follow normal songwriting or genre expectations.

label: Rock---Folk Metal
description: Metal blended with folk melodies, instruments, themes, or regional musical elements.
classificationHint: Use this when heavy metal arrangement and folk identity are both central.

label: Rock---Folk Rock
description: Rock music blended with folk songwriting, acoustic instruments, and narrative or traditional influence.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is rock-band based but folk melody or acoustic songwriting is central.

label: Rock---Funeral Doom Metal
description: Extremely slow doom metal with bleak atmosphere, long structures, and a funeral-like heaviness.
classificationHint: Use this when doom metal is especially slow, massive, and mournful.

label: Rock---Funk Metal
description: Metal or hard rock with funk basslines, syncopated grooves, and rhythmic guitar attack.
classificationHint: Use this when funk groove is central inside a heavy rock or metal arrangement.

label: Rock---Garage Rock
description: Raw, energetic rock with simple riffs, rough production, and a direct live-band feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track sounds primitive, gritty, and performance-driven rather than polished.

label: Rock---Glam
description: Rock with flamboyant presentation, catchy hooks, theatrical style, and often 1970s glam influence.
classificationHint: Use this when the track combines rock riffs with theatrical, flashy, or glittery pop appeal.

label: Rock---Goregrind
description: Extreme grindcore/death metal style with very harsh vocals, fast drums, and gore-themed aesthetics.
classificationHint: Use this only when the track is extreme, grinding, and gore/death-metal oriented.

label: Rock---Goth Rock
description: Dark post-punk-derived rock with gothic atmosphere, deep or dramatic vocals, and shadowy guitar textures.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is guitar-band based and gothic rather than synth-centered darkwave.

label: Rock---Gothic Metal
description: Metal with dark romantic atmosphere, gothic melody, and often dramatic or operatic vocals.
classificationHint: Use this when metal heaviness combines with gothic mood rather than pure extreme-metal aggression.

label: Rock---Grindcore
description: Extremely fast and aggressive punk/metal style with blast beats, short songs, and harsh vocals.
classificationHint: Use this when speed, brevity, and abrasive extremity dominate.

label: Rock---Groove Metal
description: Metal focused on mid-tempo rhythmic riffs, heavy groove, and strong downbeat impact.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is heavy but more groove-driven than fast or technical.

label: Rock---Grunge
description: Alternative rock with heavy guitars, raw emotion, and a darker, sludgy or punk-influenced 1990s feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track combines alternative rock songwriting with distorted, gritty heaviness.

label: Rock---Hard Rock
description: Rock with heavier guitars, strong drums, forceful vocals, and riff-driven energy.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is heavier than standard rock but not clearly metal.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Heavy Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Heavy Metal is usually darker, more riff-metal oriented, and heavier; Hard Rock stays closer to rock.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Classic Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: Classic Rock is broader and often less heavy.

label: Rock---Hardcore
description: Fast, aggressive punk-derived rock with shouted vocals, short direct songs, and high physical intensity.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is hardcore punk or hardcore rock rather than electronic hardcore.

label: Rock---Heavy Metal
description: Classic broad metal style with heavy riffs, powerful vocals, and strong guitar-centered structure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is metal but no more specific metal subtype is clearly dominant.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Hard Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: Hard Rock is less heavy and less metal-riff focused.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Power Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Power Metal is faster, more melodic, and more heroic.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Thrash
distinguishFrom.difference: Thrash is faster and more aggressive.

label: Rock---Horror Rock
description: Rock with horror themes, theatrical darkness, and macabre imagery.
classificationHint: Use this when the track's identity is strongly horror-themed rather than simply gothic or heavy.

label: Rock---Indie Rock
description: Guitar-based rock with independent or alternative aesthetics, often less polished or more personal than mainstream rock.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is rock-band based and indie-oriented rather than pop-first.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Indie Pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Indie Pop is more melody and pop-hook focused; Indie Rock is more guitar/band driven.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Alternative Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: Alternative Rock is broader and can be heavier or more mainstream.

label: Rock---Industrial
description: Rock with mechanical rhythms, harsh textures, and industrial atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when a rock arrangement uses industrial sound design but is not necessarily metal-heavy.

label: Rock---Industrial Metal
description: Metal using mechanical rhythms, industrial electronics, samples, and harsh machine-like production.
classificationHint: Use this when metal guitars and industrial programming are both central.

label: Rock---J-Rock
description: Japanese rock, often combining rock-band instrumentation with Japanese pop, anime, visual-kei, or alternative influences.
classificationHint: Use this for Japanese rock tracks that are clearly band-driven rather than general J-pop.

label: Rock---Jangle Pop
description: Guitar pop with bright, ringing guitars, melodic songwriting, and a light indie/rock feel.
classificationHint: Use this when clean chiming guitars are the defining feature.

label: Rock---K-Rock
description: Korean rock music with rock-band instrumentation and Korean pop or alternative-rock context.
classificationHint: Use this for Korean rock tracks rather than general K-pop.

label: Rock---Krautrock
description: Experimental German rock with motorik rhythms, repetition, improvisation, and electronic or psychedelic influence.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has hypnotic German experimental-rock character.

label: Rock---Lo-Fi
description: Rock or indie music with deliberately rough, home-recorded, or low-fidelity production.
classificationHint: Use this when the recording texture itself feels raw, small, or intentionally unpolished.

label: Rock---Lounge
description: Smooth, relaxed rock/pop-adjacent music with stylish, easygoing, or retro cocktail atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels lounge-like rather than direct rock performance.

label: Rock---Math Rock
description: Rock with complex rhythms, unusual meters, intricate guitar patterns, and precise arrangement.
classificationHint: Use this when rhythmic complexity and angular guitar interplay are central.

label: Rock---Melodic Death Metal
description: Death metal that emphasizes melodic guitar lines, harmonized riffs, and structured songwriting.
classificationHint: Use this when death metal harshness is combined with strong melodic guitar identity.

label: Rock---Melodic Hardcore
description: Hardcore punk with stronger melody, emotional vocals, and more tuneful guitar movement.
classificationHint: Use this when hardcore intensity is present but the songwriting is more melodic and expressive.

label: Rock---Metalcore
description: Metal and hardcore hybrid with heavy riffs, screamed vocals, breakdowns, and modern production.
classificationHint: Use this when hardcore breakdown structure and metal riffing are both central.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Deathcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Deathcore is more death-metal influenced and often more extreme.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Melodic Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Melodic Hardcore is more punk/hardcore and less metal-riff oriented.

label: Rock---Mod
description: 1960s-influenced British pop-rock style with sharp rhythms, clean presentation, and R&B/soul influence.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has mod-era British rock/pop character.

label: Rock---NDW
description: Neue Deutsche Welle: German new wave with quirky vocals, synths or guitars, and late-1970s/1980s character.
classificationHint: Use this for German-language new wave or quirky post-punk/synth-pop tracks.

label: Rock---Neofolk
description: Dark or post-industrial folk-rock with acoustic instruments, ritual mood, and often solemn vocals.
classificationHint: Use this when folk instrumentation and dark alternative/industrial atmosphere combine.

label: Rock---New Wave
description: Pop-oriented post-punk and rock with synths, angular guitars, and late-1970s/1980s modernity.
classificationHint: Use this when the track mixes rock-band structure with new-wave style or synth-era pop energy.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---New Wave
distinguishFrom.difference: Electronic New Wave emphasizes synth/electronic production; Rock New Wave is more band-oriented.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Post-Punk
distinguishFrom.difference: Post-Punk is usually darker or more angular.

label: Rock---No Wave
description: Aggressive experimental rock rejecting conventional melody and rock structure, often noisy and confrontational.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is deliberately anti-rock, abrasive, and avant-garde.

label: Rock---Noise
description: Rock using abrasive feedback, distortion, and noise texture as a central musical element.
classificationHint: Use this when harsh guitar or feedback textures dominate the rock arrangement.

label: Rock---Noisecore
description: Extreme hardcore/noise style with chaotic blasts, harsh vocals, and very abrasive short-form intensity.
classificationHint: Use this only for highly chaotic, noisy hardcore extremes.

label: Rock---Nu Metal
description: Modern metal style combining heavy riffs, groove, hip-hop influence, and alternative-metal production.
classificationHint: Use this when downtuned riffs, groove, rap/angsty vocals, and late-1990s/2000s metal character are present.

label: Rock---Oi
description: Street-punk style with shouted choruses, simple riffs, and working-class punk identity.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has direct chant-like punk energy and Oi/street-punk character.

label: Rock---Parody
description: Rock music created to imitate or mock another artist, song, or style.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is rock-based and its main purpose is comic or satirical imitation.

label: Rock---Pop Punk
description: Fast, melodic punk rock with catchy choruses, youthful energy, and accessible pop structure.
classificationHint: Use this when punk rhythm and guitars are combined with clear pop hooks.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Punk
distinguishFrom.difference: Punk is rawer and less pop-hook oriented; Pop Punk is catchier and more melodic.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Emo
distinguishFrom.difference: Emo is more emotionally expressive and less purely upbeat pop-punk.

label: Rock---Pop Rock
description: Rock music with accessible pop songwriting, clear hooks, and mainstream melodic structure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is guitar/band based but more pop-oriented than hard or alternative rock.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Indie Pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Indie Pop is defined by an independent or alternative pop aesthetic; Pop Rock is defined by combining pop hooks with a rock-band arrangement.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Alternative Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: Alternative Rock allows rougher, heavier, or less conventional songwriting; Pop Rock prioritizes concise hooks and mainstream pop structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Vocal
distinguishFrom.difference: Vocal is a broad pop label centered on the singer; Pop Rock additionally requires prominent rock instrumentation and band-oriented arrangement.

label: Rock---Pornogrind
description: Extreme grindcore-related style with explicit sexual themes, harsh vocals, and abrasive speed.
classificationHint: Use this only when the track clearly fits that extreme grindcore niche.

label: Rock---Post Rock
description: Rock using guitars and band instrumentation for atmosphere, build-ups, and texture rather than conventional song structure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is instrumental or expansive, with gradual crescendos and cinematic mood.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Score
distinguishFrom.difference: Score is media-functional; Post Rock is a band-based style with crescendos and atmosphere.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Shoegaze
distinguishFrom.difference: Shoegaze is more vocal/guitar-wall and song-texture oriented.

label: Rock---Post-Hardcore
description: Hardcore-derived rock with more complex structures, melody, dynamics, and emotional or experimental range.
classificationHint: Use this when hardcore aggression is present but the arrangement is more expansive or varied.

label: Rock---Post-Metal
description: Metal using post-rock-like atmosphere, long structures, heavy crescendos, and textural development.
classificationHint: Use this when metal heaviness is combined with slow atmospheric build and expansive form.

label: Rock---Post-Punk
description: Rock after punk that adds darker atmosphere, angular rhythm, bass-driven grooves, or experimental structure.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has punk roots but colder, more artful, or more atmospheric execution.

label: Rock---Power Metal
description: Melodic metal with fast rhythms, soaring vocals, heroic themes, and bright guitar harmonies.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is metal but strongly melodic, uplifting, and dramatic.

label: Rock---Power Pop
description: Guitar pop-rock with strong melodies, bright harmonies, and concise catchy songwriting.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has rock guitars but the main identity is melodic pop craft.

label: Rock---Power Violence
description: Extreme hardcore punk style with abrupt tempo changes, blasts, short songs, and chaotic aggression.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is faster and more chaotic than normal hardcore but still punk-rooted.

label: Rock---Prog Rock
description: Rock with extended structures, complex musicianship, changing sections, and ambitious composition.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is rock-based and progressive in arrangement or concept.

label: Rock---Progressive Metal
description: Metal with complex composition, technical playing, unusual structures, and progressive-rock influence.
classificationHint: Use this when metal heaviness combines with extended form and technical/progressive writing.

label: Rock---Psychedelic Rock
description: Rock with dreamy, surreal, or mind-expanding sound, often using effects, improvisation, and unusual textures.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a psychedelic rock identity rather than just retro rock sound.

label: Rock---Psychobilly
description: Fast rockabilly mixed with punk energy and horror or outsider themes.
classificationHint: Use this when upright-bass rockabilly sound is combined with punk speed or horror attitude.

label: Rock---Pub Rock
description: Straightforward, rootsy rock performed with small-club energy and stripped-down arrangements.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels direct, unpretentious, and bar-band oriented.

label: Rock---Punk
description: Fast, direct rock with simple riffs, raw vocals, and rebellious energy.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is punk rock but not more specifically hardcore, pop punk, Oi, or post-punk.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Hardcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardcore is faster, more aggressive, and more shouted.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Pop Punk
distinguishFrom.difference: Pop Punk is catchier and more melodic.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Oi
distinguishFrom.difference: Oi is chant-like street punk with a specific working-class style.

label: Rock---Rock & Roll
description: Early rock style built from rhythm and blues, swing, simple guitar/piano riffs, and danceable energy.
classificationHint: Use this for classic 1950s-style rock and roll or clearly retro rock-and-roll tracks.

label: Rock---Rock Opera
description: Rock music arranged as part of a larger dramatic or narrative work.
classificationHint: Use this when the track belongs to or strongly resembles a theatrical concept-rock narrative.

label: Rock---Rockabilly
description: Early rock and roll blended with country, slap bass, twangy guitar, and energetic vocal style.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has clear 1950s rockabilly rhythm and instrumentation.

label: Rock---Shoegaze
description: Atmospheric rock with dense guitar effects, blurred vocals, and walls of reverb or distortion.
classificationHint: Use this when texture and guitar haze are more important than clear riffs or vocal hooks.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Dream Pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dream Pop is softer and clearer; Shoegaze is denser and more guitar-effect saturated.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Noise
distinguishFrom.difference: Noise Rock is more abrasive; Shoegaze is more hazy and melodic.

label: Rock---Ska
description: Rock or punk connected to ska's offbeat rhythm, horn accents, and upbeat dance feel.
classificationHint: Use this when rock-band energy is combined with ska rhythm.

label: Rock---Skiffle
description: Early folk-blues-influenced British pop/rock style using simple acoustic or homemade instrumentation.
classificationHint: Use this for skiffle-style rootsy early rock/folk performance.

label: Rock---Sludge Metal
description: Slow, heavy metal combining doom weight with hardcore or noise-rock aggression.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels thick, dirty, slow-to-mid tempo, and crushing.

label: Rock---Soft Rock
description: Gentle, melodic rock with smooth production, softer vocals, and accessible songwriting.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is clearly rock-based but restrained and radio-friendly.

label: Rock---Southern Rock
description: Rock with blues, country, and American Southern influences, often guitar-driven and rootsy.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a southern US rock character.

label: Rock---Space Rock
description: Rock with cosmic atmosphere, extended jams, synth effects, and psychedelic spaciousness.
classificationHint: Use this when the track feels spacey, expansive, and rock-based.

label: Rock---Speed Metal
description: Fast traditional metal with rapid riffs, energetic drumming, and high-speed guitar attack.
classificationHint: Use this when classic metal vocabulary is played with strong speed emphasis.

label: Rock---Stoner Rock
description: Heavy, riff-based rock with fuzzy guitar tone, laid-back groove, and psychedelic or desert-rock feel.
classificationHint: Use this when thick fuzz riffs and heavy groove dominate without becoming extreme metal.

label: Rock---Surf
description: Guitar rock with reverb-heavy lead lines, fast picking, and beach or surf-culture feel.
classificationHint: Use this for surf rock instrumentals or songs with clear surf guitar style.

label: Rock---Swamp Pop
description: Roots-pop or rock style blending Louisiana rhythm and blues, country, and emotional ballad feel.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has swampy Louisiana pop/rock character.

label: Rock---Symphonic Rock
description: Rock using orchestral arrangements, symphonic scale, or classical-style instrumentation.
classificationHint: Use this when rock structure is combined with orchestral or symphonic presentation.

label: Rock---Technical Death Metal
description: Death metal emphasizing complex riffs, precise musicianship, irregular rhythms, and high technical skill.
classificationHint: Use this when death metal aggression is combined with clear technical complexity.

label: Rock---Thrash
description: Fast, aggressive metal with tight riffing, rapid picking, and punk-influenced intensity.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has classic thrash metal speed and riff attack.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Speed Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Speed Metal is usually cleaner and closer to traditional heavy metal; Thrash is more aggressive and punk-influenced.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---Death Metal
distinguishFrom.difference: Death Metal is heavier, growlier, and more brutal.

label: Rock---Twist
description: Early 1960s dance-rock style built around a simple, upbeat rhythm for the twist dance.
classificationHint: Use this when the track clearly has twist-era dance-rock feel.

label: Rock---Viking Metal
description: Metal with Norse, Viking, or epic folk themes, often combining extreme or folk metal elements.
classificationHint: Use this when the track's metal identity is strongly tied to Viking/Norse atmosphere or themes.

label: Rock---Yé-Yé
description: 1960s French pop-rock style with youthful vocals, catchy melodies, and playful European pop character.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a French 1960s girl-pop or beat-pop feel.

label: Stage & Screen---Musical
description: Music written or arranged for musical theatre, where songs carry character, scene, or narrative function.
classificationHint: Use this when the track clearly sounds like a theatre musical number rather than a standalone pop, classical, or soundtrack piece.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Soundtrack
distinguishFrom.difference: Soundtrack is broader media music; Musical specifically implies sung theatre-style numbers and dramatic performance.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---Vocal
distinguishFrom.difference: Vocal pop is standalone song-oriented; Musical vocals are usually theatrical and narrative-driven.

label: Stage & Screen---Score
description: Instrumental or orchestral music composed to support film, television, games, or other visual media.
classificationHint: Use this when the track functions like background or dramatic underscore rather than a standalone song.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Soundtrack
distinguishFrom.difference: Soundtrack can include songs and compiled tracks; Score specifically means composed underscore.

distinguishFrom.label: Classical---Modern
distinguishFrom.difference: Modern classical is a concert/classical category; Score is defined by media function.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Modern Classical
distinguishFrom.difference: Modern Classical describes musical language; Score describes use in screen or stage context.

label: Stage & Screen---Soundtrack
description: Music associated with film, television, games, theatre, or other media, including both songs and instrumental pieces.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is best understood by its media context rather than by a single musical style.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Score
distinguishFrom.difference: Score is specifically composed underscore; Soundtrack is broader and can include songs.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Theme
distinguishFrom.difference: Theme is a recognizable title or character motif; Soundtrack is the broader category.

label: Stage & Screen---Theme
description: A recognizable theme tune or recurring musical identity for a film, series, game, character, or show.
classificationHint: Use this when the track is short or strongly motif-based and works as a title, character, or program theme.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Soundtrack
distinguishFrom.difference: Soundtrack is broader; Theme is a specific recognizable motif or title piece.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Score
distinguishFrom.difference: Score may include many underscore cues; Theme is usually the central identifiable musical idea.

label: Electronic---Drumstep
description: A bass-music hybrid that combines drum-and-bass speed and breakbeat detail with the heavy, half-time impact and sound design associated with dubstep.
classificationHint: Use this when fast DnB-scale pacing coexists with a pronounced half-time drop, syncopated bass design, or dubstep-style weight.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass normally sustains a fast two-step breakbeat feel; Drumstep foregrounds half-time impact and dubstep-derived drop structure.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dubstep
distinguishFrom.difference: Dubstep usually centers on a roughly 140 BPM half-time framework; Drumstep adds faster DnB pacing or breakbeat movement.

label: Electronic---Electronic Pop
description: Pop songwriting built around clearly electronic production, with prominent synthesizers, programmed drums, processed vocals, and concise hooks.
classificationHint: Use this when verse-chorus pop structure and vocal hooks remain central while electronic instrumentation defines most of the arrangement.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Synth-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Synth-pop specifically foregrounds synthesizer-led pop aesthetics; Electronic Pop is the broader modern category for pop shaped by electronic production.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop prioritizes a dancefloor-ready pulse; Electronic Pop can be slower or less club-oriented while retaining electronic production.

label: Electronic---Electronic Trap
description: Festival-oriented electronic bass music that adapts trap's 808 sub-bass, rapid hi-hat figures, and half-time groove to build-and-drop arrangements.
classificationHint: Use this when trap-derived drums and 808 weight drive an instrumental EDM arrangement with pronounced builds, drops, and synthesized leads or basses.

distinguishFrom.label: Hip Hop---Trap
distinguishFrom.difference: Hip-hop Trap is organized around rap production and vocal song form; Electronic Trap emphasizes EDM builds, drops, and instrumental impact.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dubstep
distinguishFrom.difference: Dubstep uses syncopated bass-music rhythms rooted in UK garage and dub; Electronic Trap is identified by 808s, trap hi-hats, and trap-derived drum programming.

label: Electronic---Liquid Drum n Bass
description: The melodic and soulful side of drum and bass, pairing fast rolling breaks and sub-bass with warm harmony, atmosphere, vocals, or jazz- and soul-influenced instrumentation.
classificationHint: Use this when unmistakable DnB rhythm and tempo are softened by flowing melodies, lush harmony, emotional vocals, or an atmospheric and polished tone.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass is the broad parent style; Liquid Drum n Bass specifically emphasizes melody, warmth, atmosphere, and soulful musicality.

label: Electronic---Nightcore
description: A sped-up edit style that raises both tempo and pitch, typically giving existing pop, dance, or electronic songs brighter vocals and more urgent energy.
classificationHint: Use this for an existing song audibly accelerated with corresponding pitch-raised vocals; do not use it merely because an original track is naturally fast or high-pitched.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Speedcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Speedcore is an original extreme-hardcore genre defined by very high tempo and aggressive kicks; Nightcore is primarily a speed-and-pitch transformation of another song.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dance-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Dance-pop describes the underlying songwriting and dance production; Nightcore describes a sped-up, pitch-raised version and may be combined with the base style.

label: Electronic---Nightstep
description: An internet remix label for dubstep or closely related bass music presented with the accelerated tempo, raised pitch, and bright vocal character associated with Nightcore.
classificationHint: Use this only when both sides are audible: dubstep-derived bass or half-time drops and a clear Nightcore-style speed-and-pitch treatment.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Nightcore
distinguishFrom.difference: Nightcore can transform music of many styles; Nightstep specifically retains prominent dubstep or bass-music traits.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Dubstep
distinguishFrom.difference: Dubstep alone does not imply raised pitch or accelerated source audio; Nightstep combines that bass framework with Nightcore-style processing.

label: Electronic---UK Bounce
description: An upbeat UK hard-dance style related to Scouse House and Donk, driven by four-on-the-floor kicks, springy offbeat bass, bright riffs, and energetic vocal samples.
classificationHint: Use this when a fast, cheerful hard-house groove is dominated by a distinctly bouncy or donk-like offbeat bass rather than a hardstyle kick sequence.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Donk
distinguishFrom.difference: Donk highlights the characteristic metallic offbeat bass sound; UK Bounce is the broader regional dance style that commonly uses it.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Hardstyle
distinguishFrom.difference: Hardstyle centers on distorted, pitched kicks and dramatic hard-dance structure; UK Bounce favors a lighter springing bass groove and more playful presentation.

label: Electronic---Neurofunk
description: A dark, technically intricate drum-and-bass style evolved from techstep, centered on continuously modulated bass design, precise drums, dense processing, and a tense futuristic atmosphere.
classificationHint: Use this when fast DnB rhythm supports complex moving bass timbres, tightly engineered percussion, and a darker, more mechanical sound than conventional dancefloor DnB.

distinguishFrom.label: Electronic---Drum n Bass
distinguishFrom.difference: Drum n Bass is the broad parent style; Neurofunk specifically foregrounds dark, highly modulated bass sound design and technical rhythmic detail.

label: Pop---Anime
description: A context category for vocal themes, insert songs, image songs, and related releases created for or strongly identified with Japanese anime and adjacent media.
classificationHint: Use this when the track has a documented anime-media role or unmistakable anisong context; combine it with J-pop, Pop Rock, J-Rock, or another style that describes the actual sound.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---J-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: J-pop describes Japanese popular music as a musical market and style family; Anime describes media context, and the two may overlap without being interchangeable.

distinguishFrom.label: Stage & Screen---Soundtrack
distinguishFrom.difference: Soundtrack broadly covers music associated with screen and stage media; Anime specifically identifies the Japanese animation and related-media context.

label: Pop---C-pop
description: An umbrella category for Chinese popular music, especially Mandarin, Cantonese, and other Chinese-language pop traditions across Greater China and its diaspora.
classificationHint: Use this when Chinese-language or Chinese-market pop identity is central; combine it with Ballad, Dance-pop, R&B, or another tag that describes the track's musical form.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---J-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: C-pop denotes Chinese-language and Chinese-market popular music; J-pop denotes Japanese popular music.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---K-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: C-pop denotes Chinese-language and Chinese-market popular music; K-pop denotes the South Korean pop industry and its associated repertoire.

label: Pop---T-Pop
description: Thai popular music shaped by local language and culture while drawing on contemporary pop, dance, R&B, hip-hop, rock, and idol-group production.
classificationHint: Use this when Thai-language or Thai-market pop identity is central; combine it with Dance-pop, Contemporary R&B, Pop Rock, or another tag for the audible style.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---J-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: T-Pop identifies Thai popular music and cultural context; J-pop identifies Japanese popular music.

distinguishFrom.label: Pop---K-pop
distinguishFrom.difference: Modern T-Pop may borrow K-pop production and idol presentation, but remains rooted in Thailand's language, artists, and music industry.

label: Rock---C-Rock
description: An umbrella category for rock from Chinese-language scenes, spanning mainstream pop rock, alternative bands, heavier styles, and regionally specific songwriting.
classificationHint: Use this when Chinese-language or Chinese-scene identity is relevant and guitars, live-band arrangement, or rock vocal delivery are central; add the more specific rock style when known.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---J-Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: C-Rock identifies Chinese-language and Chinese-scene rock; J-Rock identifies Japanese rock scenes and repertoire.

distinguishFrom.label: Rock---K-Rock
distinguishFrom.difference: C-Rock identifies Chinese-language and Chinese-scene rock; K-Rock identifies South Korean rock scenes and repertoire.
